pājiyamānāpi.meaning_2: being driven forward; being caused to go
pājiyamānāpi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Present participle masculine plural of pājeti, causative of ajati. In the text with -pi: 'even when being driven forward'. The sequence -āpi is the emphatic particle; the headword is pājiyamāna.
pājiyamānāpi.example_1: Athassa goṇā taṃ ṭhānaṃ patvā dhuraṃ chaḍḍesuṃ, punappunaṃ āropetvā pājiyamānāpi purato na gacchiṃsu.
pājiyamānāpi.translation_1: Again and again he tried to drive them forward, but they refused.

heti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Future of hoti according to PEU heti2; possibly a variant spelling or sandhi. No sentence context supplied.

paṭijinitvā.meaning_2: having defeated in return; having won back; having overcome again
paṭijinitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in -tvā of paṭijināti (paṭi + √ji 1). In the text it is part of the potter's demand: having won back what the boys took, give it to me. Sometimes analysed with a second √ji, but the -nā- form points to √ji 1.
paṭijinitvā.example_1: Ime maṃ dārakā bahuṃ lakkhaṃ jiniṃsu, taṃ me paṭijinitvā dehī ’’ ti āha.
paṭijinitvā.translation_1: The foster-brother went and told the potter to finish the job given by his father.

lañchāpetvā.meaning_2: having had (it) stamped; having had (it) marked; having had (it) sealed
lañchāpetvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative absolutive of lañchāpeti; in these sentences, used of ordering a house to be marked or sealed. The PEU analysis lañcha + ṇāpe + tvā agrees.
lañchāpetvā.example_1: Rājā kujjhitvā gehaṃ lañchāpetvā seṭṭhiñca bhariyañca hatthe gahetvā bahi kārāpesi.
lañchāpetvā.translation_1: The King became angry, had the house sealed, and taking the merchant and his wife by the hand, had them turned out.
lañchāpetvā.example_2: Atha ‘ na mayaṃ dassāmā ’ ti vutte gharaṃ lañchāpetvā amhe bahi kārāpesī ’’ ti.
lañchāpetvā.translation_2: “Then, when we said, ‘We will not give her up,’ he had the house sealed and had us turned out.”

vikkhālāpetvā.meaning_2: having made (someone) wash (the mouth); having had (the mouth) rinsed
vikkhālāpetvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative absolutive; in the sentence with mukhaṃ it means having had the infants' mouths washed. PEU splits as vi + khala + ṇāpe + tvā.
vikkhālāpetvā.example_1: Antamaso thanapāyinopi dārake mukhaṃ vikkhālāpetvā catumadhuraṃ mukhe pakkhipāpetvā mahāseṭṭhi uposathike kāreti.
vikkhālāpetvā.translation_1: “Even the nursing infants have their mouths washed and are given the four sweet foods to eat, and so the great rich man has them keep the Uposatha.”

tepissa.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of te (pronoun) + assa (pronoun, dative/genitive singular of ta). In the text tepissa = te + pi + assa, with the emphatic particle pi inserted; the entry covers the sandhi of te + assa. The -ss- is written single after the elided vowel.
tepissa.example_1: Evaṃ pasaṃsiyabhāvaṃ āpajjitvā jīvitapariyosāne tāvatiṃsabhavane sakko devarājā hutvā nibbatti, tepissa sahāyakā tattheva nibbattiṃsu, vaḍḍhakī vissakammadevaputto hutvā nibbatti.
tepissa.translation_1: Having thus attained a praiseworthy state, at the end of his life he was reborn in the Tāvatiṃsa heaven as Sakka, the Lord of the Devas. His companions were also reborn there, and the carpenter was reborn as Vissakamma, the son of the devas.
tepissa.example_2: ‘‘ Bhadde, mā etaṃ kathehi, mayaṃ tena saddhiṃ ekadivasaṃ sukhayānake nisīditvā nhāyituṃ nikkhantā nevassa gatiṃ jānāma, ito cito ca vicaritvā taṃ adisvā mātāpitūnaṃ ārocayimhā, tepissa roditvā kanditvā petakiccaṃ kiriṃsū ’’ ti.
tepissa.translation_2: “Good lady, do not speak of him. We drove out of the city in a comfortable carriage with him one day, and we do not know where he went. We searched everywhere and, failing to find him, informed his mother and father; they wept and lamented, and performed the rites for the dead.”

uppaṇḍetvā.meaning_2: having mocked; having ridiculed; having made fun of
uppaṇḍetvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive from uppaṇḍeti; in the text it describes the companions' mockery of the woman.
uppaṇḍetvā.example_1: Puna sakko tassā santikaṃ gantvā,‘‘ diṭṭhā te sahāyikā ’’ ti vatvā ‘‘ diṭṭhā maṃ uppaṇḍetvā gatā, tattheva maṃ nehī ’’ ti vutte taṃ tattheva netvā udake vissajjetvā,‘‘ diṭṭhā te tāsaṃ sampattī ’’ ti pucchi.
uppaṇḍetvā.translation_1: Sakka went to her again and asked, 'Have you seen your companions?' Having said, 'I have seen them; they ridiculed me and went away; take me back to that mountain-cave,' when she had spoken, he took her back to that very place, released her in the water, and asked, 'Have you seen the splendor of those companions?'

sippalivanaṃ.meaning_2: silk-cotton forest; forest of silk-cotton trees
sippalivanaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text. sippali is the silk-cotton (red cotton) tree (Bombax ceiba); vana means forest.
sippalivanaṃ.example_1: Athassa sippalivanaṃ sampattakāle rathasaddaṃ sutvā bhītā garuḷapotakā viraviṃsu.
sippalivanaṃ.translation_1: When he reached the silk-cotton forest, the young garuḍas heard the chariot sound, were terrified, and cried out.

rukkhālake.meaning_2: wooden vice; clamp for straightening wood|wooden straightener
rukkhālake.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Used in the simile of the fletcher straightening an arrow: a wooden vice or clamp. Locative singular in the text.
rukkhālake.example_1: Usukārova tejananti yathā nāma usukāro araññato ekaṃ vaṅkadaṇḍakaṃ āharitvā nittacaṃ katvā kañjiyatelena makkhetvā aṅgārakapalle tāpetvā rukkhālake uppīḷetvā nivaṅkaṃ ujuṃ vālavijjhanayoggaṃ karoti, katvā ca pana rājarājamahāmattānaṃ sippaṃ dassetvā mahantaṃ sakkārasammānaṃ labhati, evameva medhāvī paṇḍito viññū puriso phandanādisabhāvametaṃ cittaṃ dhutaṅgāraññāvāsavasena, nittacaṃ apagataoḷārikakilesaṃ katvā saddhāsinehena temetvā kāyikacetasikavīriyena tāpetvā samathavipassanālake uppīḷetvā ujuṃ akuṭilaṃ nibbisevanaṃ karoti, katvā ca pana saṅkhāre sammasitvā mahantaṃ avijjakkhandhaṃ padāletvā,‘‘ tisso vijjā, cha abhiññā, nava lokuttaradhamme ’’ ti imaṃ visesaṃ hatthagatameva katvā aggadakkhiṇeyyabhāvaṃ labhati.
rukkhālake.translation_1: ‘Just as a fletcher makes an arrow straight’ means: just as a fletcher takes a crooked piece of wood from the forest, peels it, coats it with oil, heats it over a bed of coals, presses it in a straightener, and makes it straight and fit for piercing—and having done so, shows his skill to kings and ministers and receives great honor—even so, the wise, astute, and observant person makes this mind, which has the nature of agitation and so on, straight, uncrooked, and free from piercing by making it free from coarse defilements through the practice of residing in the forest with dhutaṅga practices, softening it with the moisture of faith, heating it with bodily and mental energy, and pressing it in the straightener of calm and insight. Having done this, and having contemplated the formations and broken through the great mass of ignorance, he attains the three true knowledges, the six supernormal powers, and the nine supramundane qualities, and having held this special state in his hand, he attains the status of one who is worthy of the highest offerings.

okamokataubbhatoti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In compound with oka + amoka + ta, ends the phrase; 'yāva okā amokā ubbhato' means 'from the lair and not-the-lair drawn out'. Nominative singular of ubbhata.

satame.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Ordinal from sata (hundred). In the text it appears as satamaṃ (accusative singular) and satame (locative singular).
satame.example_1: ‘‘ Atthi nu kho evaṃ saṃsāre saṃsarantiyā mama puttassa upakāro katapubbo ’’ ti upadhārayamānā tato uttariṃ satamaṃ attabhāvaṃ anussaritvā satame attabhāve mayā etassa pādaparicārikāya hutvā etasmiṃ jīvitā voropanaṭṭhāne jīvitadānaṃ dinnaṃ, aho mayā mama puttassa mahāupakāro katapubbo ’’ ti gehe nisinnāva uttariṃ visesetvā ‘‘ upadhārethā ’’ ti āha.
satame.translation_1: Considering, 'Has she rendered a support to my son while he was wandering in the round of existences?' she recalled the hundredth existence. 'In that hundredth existence, I was his attendant, and in that place where I could have deprived him of life, I gave him the gift of life; oh, I have rendered a great support to my son,' she thought, and while still sitting in her house, she said, 'Consider further [and discern the matter].'

sacesi.meaning_2: if you are; if you wish
sacesi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of sace + asi (√as 1, 2nd singular). In the text: 'if you desire to be released from suffering'. Sometimes written sace 'si. Alternative analysis sace + si gives a different meaning, but 'asi' fits the context.
sacesi.example_1: ‘‘ Sādhāvuso, sacesi dukkhā muccitukāmo, salākabhattaṃ dehi, pakkhikabhattaṃ dehi, vassāvāsikaṃ dehi, cīvarādayo paccaye dehi, attano sāpateyyaṃ tayo koṭṭhāse katvā ekena kammantaṃ payojehi, ekena puttadāraṃ posehi, ekaṃ buddhasāsane dehī ’’ ti āha.
sacesi.translation_1: 'Good, friend; if you desire to be released from suffering, give meal offerings by lots, give fortnightly offerings, give offerings for the rainy season, give requisites like robes and so on. Divide your wealth into three parts: use one part for your business, use one part to support your wife and children, and give one part to the Buddha’s dispensation,' he said.

ālassiyābhibhūto.meaning_2: overcome by laziness; oppressed by sloth; overcome by idleness
ālassiyābhibhūto.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound of ālassiya (laziness; sloth) and abhibhūta (overcome; oppressed). Nominative singular masculine in both sentences, agreeing with the subject.
ālassiyābhibhūto.example_1: So tato paṭṭhāya ukkaṇṭhito anabhirato dvattiṃsākāre sajjhāyaṃ na karoti, uddesaṃ na gaṇhāti, kiso lūkho dhamanisanthatagatto ālassiyābhibhūto kacchuparikiṇṇo ahosi.
ālassiyābhibhūto.translation_1: From that time on, he was dissatisfied and discontented; he did not rehearse the 32-fold nature, did not study the recitation; he became emaciated, shriveled up, his body covered with veins, oppressed by laziness, and covered with scabs.
ālassiyābhibhūto.example_2: Atha naṃ daharasāmaṇerā,‘‘ āvuso, kiṃ tvaṃ ṭhitaṭṭhāne ṭhitova nisinnaṭṭhāne nisinnova ahosi, paṇḍurogābhibhūto kiso lūkho dhamanisanthatagatto ālassiyābhibhūto kacchuparikiṇṇo, kiṃ te katan ’’ ti pucchiṃsu.
ālassiyābhibhūto.translation_2: Then the young bhikkhus and novices asked him, 'Friend, why are you always standing in the same standing spot, and sitting in the same sitting spot? You are pale, emaciated, shriveled up, covered with veins, overcome by laziness, and covered with scabs; what have you done?'

bījitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive form in -tvā of the causative bījeti, seen as bījitvā with weakening of e to i. Same meaning as bījayamāno in the same sentence. Some texts read vījitvā.
bījitvā.example_1: Athassāgamanabhāvaṃ disvā paccuggamanaṃ katvā pattacīvaraṃ paṭiggahetvā,‘‘ nisīdatha, bhante ’’ ti theraṃ nisīdāpetvā tālavaṇṭaṃ ādāya bījitvā pānīyaṃ datvā pāde dhovitvā taṃ sāṭakaṃ ānetvā pādamūle ṭhapetvā,‘‘ bhante, imaṃ paribhuñjathā ’’ ti vatvā bījayamāno aṭṭhāsi.
bījitvā.translation_1: On seeing the Elder's arrival, he went out to meet him, took his bowl and robe, and after seating the Elder with the words, "Pray be seated, venerable sir," he took a palmyra fan, fanned him, gave him drinking water, washed his feet, and brought that robe, laid it at his feet, and said, "Venerable sir, pray make use of this robe." Having said this, he stood fanning him.

dussaṇṭhāpito.meaning_2: hard to maintain; difficult to keep up; hard to support
dussaṇṭhāpito.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Describes gharāvāso (household life) in the text; nominative singular agreeing with the masculine noun. PEU glosses it literally as "hard to lie in".
dussaṇṭhāpito.example_1: ‘‘ dussaṇṭhāpito gharāvāso, kiṃ nu kho katvā gihibhūto jīvissāmī ’’ ti.
dussaṇṭhāpito.translation_1: “Household life is difficult to maintain; what shall I do to live as a layman?”

sampaṭicchanakajātikaṃ.meaning_2: of the nature of accepting; inclined to take in (objects)
sampaṭicchanakajātikaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Agrees with cittaṃ in the text (nominative/accusative singular neuter). Alternative analysis: sampaṭicchana + ka + jātika.
sampaṭicchanakajātikaṃ.example_1: Atha naṃ satthā ‘‘ ehi bhikkhu, mā cintayi cittaṃ nāmetaṃ dūre hontampi ārammaṇaṃ sampaṭicchanakajātikaṃ, rāgadosamohabandhanā muccanatthāya vāyamituṃ vaṭṭatī ’’ ti vatvā imaṃ gāthamāha –
sampaṭicchanakajātikaṃ.translation_1: Then the Teacher said, "Come, bhikkhu, do not worry; this mind wanders far, takes in objects, and it is fitting to strive for release from the bonds of lust, hatred, and delusion," and recited this verse—

ghuraghurāyati.meaning_2: makes a snoring sound; makes a rumbling sound; snores
ghuraghurāyati.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Onomatopoeic verb; used of the nose in the text (nāsā ghuraghurāyati).
ghuraghurāyati.example_1: Tassā nivatthasāṭako apagato hoti, mukhato ca lālā paggharati, nāsā ghuraghurāyati, mukhaṃ vivaṭṭaṃ, dantaṃ ghaṃsati, sā tassa uddhumātakasarīraṃ viya upaṭṭhāsi.
ghuraghurāyati.translation_1: Her undergarment had slipped, saliva was flowing from her mouth, her nose was snoring, her mouth was open, and she was grinding her teeth; she appeared to him like a corpse that had swollen and decayed.

paṭiukkaṇṭhito.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Nominal past participle used as an adjective. In the text nominative singular agreeing with ayaṃ. Sometimes analysed as paṭi + ukkaṇṭhita.
paṭiukkaṇṭhito.example_1: Athassa anantaragehe ṭhitā sassu taṃ tathā gacchantaṃ disvā,‘‘ ayaṃ paṭiukkaṇṭhito bhavissati, idāneva araññato āgantvā kāsāvaṃ udare bandhitvāva gehā nikkhanto vihārābhimukho gacchati, kiṃ nu kho ’’ ti gehaṃ pavisitvā niddāyamānaṃ dhītaraṃ passitvā ‘‘ imaṃ disvā so vippaṭisārī hutvā gato ’’ ti ñatvā dhītaraṃ paharitvā ‘‘ uṭṭhehi kāḷakaṇṇi, sāmiko te taṃ niddāyamānaṃ disvā vippaṭisārī hutvā gato, natthi so ito paṭṭhāya tuyhan ’’ ti āha.
paṭiukkaṇṭhito.translation_1: Now his mother-in-law, who lived in the house nearby, saw him departing in that manner and thought, “He has become discontented again; he only just returned from the forest, and now he is leaving the house running with his robes bound about his waist, heading straight for the monastery. What could be the reason?” She entered the house, saw her daughter asleep, and realized, “He saw her asleep and must have become disgusted.” She shook her daughter and said, “Rise, you wretched hag! Your husband saw you asleep, became disgusted, and left. From now on, you will not have him as a husband.”

maṃyaṃ.meaning_2: me here; me in this place
maṃyaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of maṃ (accusative of ahaṃ, 'me') + yaṃ ('here; in this place'), as the context requires ('we cannot ordain me here'). Not maṃsa. Alternative sandhi analysis: maṃ + ayaṃ.
maṃyaṃ.example_1: ‘‘ Na sakkhissāma maṃyaṃ taṃ pabbājetuṃ, kuto tuyhaṃ samaṇabhāvo, satthakanisānapāsāṇasadisaṃ tava sīsan ’’ ti.
maṃyaṃ.translation_1: “We cannot ordain you. Where is your monastic life? Your head is like a grindstone.”

atintacittassa.meaning_2: whose mind is unsatured (with lust); whose mind is not moistened (by craving)
atintacittassa.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Gloss of anavassutacitta in the commentary; genitive or dative singular in the text (atintacittassa).
atintacittassa.translation_1: “Whose mind is not afflicted” means whose mind is not saturated with lust.

kabandhāni.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text kabandhāni is nominative plural, agreeing with chinnasīsāni. The PEU treats it as both masc and nt; here neuter is followed.
kabandhāni.example_1: Tā tesu tesu rattiṭṭhānadivāṭṭhānesu ceva caṅkamanakoṭīsu ca chinnasīsāni kabandhāni dassetuṃ amanussasaddañca bhāvetuṃ ārabhiṃsu.
kabandhāni.translation_1: They began to show them headless corpses and bodiless heads in their night and day quarters and at the ends of the cloisters, and they caused them to hear the voices of non-human beings.

kāyamiṃma.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of kāyaṃ (accusative singular of kāya) and imaṃ (accusative singular of ima). The printed form kāyamiṃma is unusual; a variant reading kāyamimaṃ is likely. This is the opening line of the Kumbhūpama verse in the Dhammapada commentary.
kāyamiṃma.example_1: 40. ‘‘ Kumbhūpamaṃ kāyamiṃma viditvā, nagarūpamaṃ cittamidaṃ ṭhapetvā;
kāyamiṃma.translation_1: 40. “Having understood this body as a clay pot, having established this mind as a fortress,

putikaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Describes the body (gattaṃ) in the text; nominative singular neuter agreeing with gattaṃ.
putikaṃ.example_1: ‘‘ Bhante, evarūpassa pana arahattūpanissayasampannassa bhikkhuno kiṃ kāraṇā gattaṃ putikaṃ jātaṃ, kiṃ kāraṇā aṭṭhīni bhinnāni, kimassa kāraṇaṃ arahattassa upanissayabhāvaṃ pattan ’’ ti?
putikaṃ.translation_1: “Venerable sir, what was the reason that the body of a bhikkhu with such supporting conditions for Arahantship became festering? Why did his bones break? And what was the cause for his attainment of Arahantship?”

vikkitāvasesā.meaning_2: remaining after being sold; left over from the sale
vikkitāvasesā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Nominal compound in the text; pūtikā bhavissanti ('will rot') shows the remaining birds are the subject. Some editions read vikkitāvasesā with a long final ā, agreeing with the feminine subject.
vikkitāvasesā.example_1: Tesaṃ dinnāvasese vikkiṇāti,‘‘ vikkitāvasesā māretvā ṭhapitā pūtikā bhavissantī ’’ ti yathā uppatituṃ na sakkonti, tathā tesaṃ jaṅghaṭṭhīni ca pakkhaṭṭhīni ca bhinditvā rāsiṃ katvā ṭhapeti, te punadivase vikkiṇāti.
vikkitāvasesā.translation_1: He would sell those that remained after giving to the influential people. Fearing that those remaining after the sale would rot if killed and kept, he would break the leg bones and wing bones of those birds so they could not fly away, and keep them piled in a heap. He would sell those birds the following day.

bījuddharaṇaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is nominative singular, the object of pāpuṇi ("he underwent castration"). PEU also suggests "being beaten with a whip", which does not suit this context.
bījuddharaṇaṃ.example_1: Paradārakammaṃ katvā niraye paccitvā pakkāvasesena cuddasasu attabhāvesu purisassa pādaparicārikā itthī ahosi, sattasu attabhāvesu bījuddharaṇaṃ pāpuṇi.
bījuddharaṇaṃ.translation_1: Having committed the act of transgression with the wife of another, he suffered in hell, and due to the remainder of that deed, he was a woman, a maidservant to men, for fourteen existences, and for seven existences he suffered castration.

ajjhuttikapathaviyaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative singular in the text (ajjhuttikapathaviyaṃ = ajjhuttika + pathavī). Contrasted with bāhirapathavī.
ajjhuttikapathaviyaṃ.example_1: Satthā āgantvā,‘‘ kāya nuttha, bhikkhave, etarahi kathāya sannisinnā ’’ ti pucchitvā,‘‘ bhante, amhehi vicaritaṭṭhāne pathavikathāyā ’’ ti vutte,‘‘ bhikkhave, esā bāhirapathavī nāma, tumhehi ajjhuttikapathaviyaṃ parikammaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭatī ’’ ti vatvā imā dve gāthā abhāsi –
ajjhuttikapathaviyaṃ.translation_1: The Teacher came and asked, “Bhikkhus, what is it that you are sitting here now talking about?” and when they replied, “Venerable sir, we were talking about the earth in the places we traveled,” the Teacher said, “Bhikkhus, this is the outer earth; it is appropriate for you to perform the preliminary practice regarding the inner earth,” and he spoke these two verses —

upaṭṭhahitukāmo.meaning_2: wishing to serve; wanting to attend (on); desirous of ministering (to)
upaṭṭhahitukāmo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Desiderative adjective from upaṭṭhahituṃ (inf of upaṭṭhahati) + kāma. Nominative singular in the text, agreeing with rājā; used of the king wishing to serve the Saṅgha.
upaṭṭhahitukāmo.example_1: Athekadivasaṃ rājā uparipāsāde ṭhito antaravīthiṃ olokayamāno ‘‘ anāthapiṇḍikassa cūḷaanāthapiṇḍikassa visākhāya suppavāsāyā ’’ ti etesaṃ gehe niccaṃ bhattakiccatthāya gacchante anekasahasse bhikkhū disvā,‘‘ kahaṃ, ayyā, gacchantī ’’ ti pucchitvā,‘‘ deva, anāthapiṇḍikassa gehe niccabhattasalākabhattagilānabhattādīnaṃ atthāya devasikaṃ dve bhikkhusahassāni gacchanti, cūḷaanāthapiṇḍikassa gehe pañcasatāni, tathā visākhāya tathā suppavāsāyā ’’ ti vutte sayampi bhikkhusaṅghaṃ upaṭṭhahitukāmo vihāraṃ gantvā bhikkhusahassena saddhiṃ satthāraṃ nimantetvā sattāhaṃ sahatthā dānaṃ datvā sattame divase satthāraṃ vanditvā,‘‘ bhante, pañcahi me bhikkhusatehi saddhiṃ nibaddhaṃ bhikkhaṃ gaṇhathā ’’ ti āha.
upaṭṭhahitukāmo.translation_1: One day, while King Pasenadi stood on his upper terrace looking down into the street, he saw thousands of bhikkhus passing by on their way to breakfast at the houses of Anāthapiṇḍika, Culla Anāthapiṇḍika, Visākhā, and Suppavāsā. He asked, “Where are these noble ones going?” When informed that they were going for food, medicine, and the like, he desired to serve the Sangha and invited the Teacher and his thousand bhikkhus to his house. For seven days he served them, and on the seventh day, he worshipped the Buddha and invited him to take his meals regularly in his house with five hundred bhikkhus.

nimātā.grammar: masc, from mātar with negative prefix
nimātā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The word appears in the text next to nipitā as nimātā nipitā, meaning 'without mother and father'. It seems to be the negated form of mātar, the counterpart to nipitā. Some editions read amātā apitā instead. Here nimātā is nominative singular.
nimātā.example_1: ‘‘ amma, aññesaṃ mātāmahakulato paṇṇākāro āharīyati, mayhaṃ koci kiñci na pesesi, kiṃ tvaṃ nimātā nipitā ’’ ti?
nimātā.translation_1: “Mother, gifts are brought from the maternal families of other princes, but no one sends anything to me. Do you not have a mother or a father?”

nipitāti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text the form is nipitāti, probably ni + pitā + iti, so the entry is for nipitu. The PEU guide splits it as ni + pitu, 'fatherless'.

pesetī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative of √is (seek, wish). Written pesetī before the following quote. 3rd singular present in the text.
pesetī.example_1: Sā ‘‘ satthāraṃ disvāva gamissāmī ’’ ti jetavanaṃ pavisitvā tathāgataṃ vanditvā ṭhitā,‘‘ kahaṃ gacchasī ’’ ti vuttā ‘‘ sāmiko maṃ bhante, kulagharaṃ pesetī ’’ āha.
pesetī.translation_1: She thought, “I will see the Teacher before I go,” and entered Jetavana, bowed to the Tathāgata, and stood there. When asked, “Where are you going?” she replied, “Venerable sir, my husband is sending me to my family’s house.”

uppannadāhaḷā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Bahubbiihi compound, feminine form uppannadāhaḷā agreeing with sā (nominative singular). The reading uppannadāhaḷā seems to be a variant of uppannadohalaḷā “having pregnancy cravings arisen”. Possible alternate splitting as uppanna + dāhaḷā.
uppannadāhaḷā.example_1: Sā na cirasseva gabbhaṃ paṭilabhitvā uppannadāhaḷā ‘‘ dohaḷo me uppanno ’’ ti ārocesi.
uppannadāhaḷā.translation_1: Not long after, she became pregnant, and experiencing a craving, she informed him, “A craving has arisen in me.”

panighātasaddaṃ.meaning_2: sound of striking; noise of impact
panighātasaddaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text. Compound of panighāta (striking, impact) + sadda (sound).
panighātasaddaṃ.example_1: So rathassa ummāre panighātasaddaṃ sutvāva ‘‘ bandhulassa rathasaddo eso, ajja licchavīnaṃ bhayaṃ uppajjissatī ’’ ti āha.
panighātasaddaṃ.translation_1: He heard the sound of the chariot on the threshold and said, “That is the chariot-sound of Bandhula; today there will be fear for the Licchavis.”

ghotessatīti.meaning_2: having proclaimed; having announced; having shouted
ghotessatīti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Form is ghosetvā with the quotation particle -iti appended (ghotessatīti is likely a variant reading of ghosetvāti); the absolutive ending -tvā is here spelled -ssa in some manuscripts. Entry written for the main word without the enclitic.

parikaraṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Not the common sense 'retinue; equipment'; here the belt or waistband of a garment. Accusative singular in the text.
parikaraṃ.example_1: ‘‘ Tena hi sabbapacchimassa parikaraṃ mocethā ’’ ti.
parikaraṃ.translation_1: “Then loosen the girdle of the rearmost man.”

soḷasakkhattuṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Adverb of number and frequency, formed from soḷasa with kkhattuṃ (from khattuṃ, 'times'). In the text it modifies vijāyi.
soḷasakkhattuṃ.example_1: Sā soḷasakkhattuṃ yamake yamake putte vijāyi.
soḷasakkhattuṃ.translation_1: She gave birth to twin sons sixteen times.

pahārāpetvā.meaning_2: having caused to be struck; having had (someone) attack; having sent (men) to strike
pahārāpetvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative absolutive of paharati (pa + √har, 'strike'). Here with payuttapurisehi: 'having had the hired men strike (the border)'. Doubtful whether the root is √har 1 (carry) or √har 2 (take, seize); the simple verb paharati 'strikes' is the usual base. Absolutive, so no case.
pahārāpetvā.example_1: ‘‘ Imasmiṃ idheva ghātiyamāne garahā me uppajjissatī ’’ ti puna cintetvā payuttapurisehi paccantaṃ pahārāpetvā bandhulaṃ pakkosāpetvā,‘‘ paccanto kira kupito, tava puttehi saddhiṃ gantvā, core gaṇhāhī ’’ ti pahiṇitvā,‘‘ etthevassa dvattiṃsāya puttehi saddhiṃ sīsaṃ chinditvā āharathā ’’ ti tehi saddhiṃ aññepi samatthe mahāyodhe pesesi.
pahārāpetvā.translation_1: Thinking, “If he is killed right here, blame will fall on me,” he suborned agents to strike the border, then summoned Bandhula, saying, “The border is in revolt; take your sons and capture the robbers,” and sent him along with powerful warriors, saying, “Cut off the heads of Bandhula and his thirty-two sons in that place and bring them to me.”

āvāsāpetvā.meaning_2: having caused to dwell; having made habitable; having settled
āvāsāpetvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive of the causative āvāsāpeti (√vas 1, causative sign *āpe). In the text it is followed by saṇṭhāpetvā: 'having made inhabitable and established'.
āvāsāpetvā.example_1: So taṃ padesaṃ āvāsāpetvā saṇṭhāpetvā nivatti.
āvāsāpetvā.translation_1: Bandhula made the region habitable and returned.

vicināpetvā.meaning_2: having caused to search; having had (it) searched; having investigated
vicināpetvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative absolutive of vicināpeti (causative of vicinati). Here with saraṃ: 'having had the lake searched'. The PEU split vi+ci+nā+ṇāpe+tvā supports the causative analysis.
vicināpetvā.example_1: Tasmiṃ aticirāyante saraṃ vicināpetvā dīpālokena purisabbhantarānipi oloketvā adisvā ‘‘ gato bhavissatī ’’ ti pakkāmi.
vicināpetvā.translation_1: When he had tarried excessively long, he had the lake searched by lamplight, and even checked the inside of his followers’ clothes, but seeing him nowhere, he thought, “He must have gone,” and left.

patipūjikakumārivatthu.meaning_2: case of the girl Patipūjikā; the story of the maiden Patipūjikā
patipūjikakumārivatthu.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the fourth story in the Dhammapada commentary. Patipūjikā is the name of the girl; kumāra here means a young woman, maiden. Nominative singular in the text.
patipūjikakumārivatthu.translation_1: 4. The Story of the Maiden Patipūjikā.
patipūjikakumārivatthu.translation_2: The story of Patipūjikā, the fourth.

vikkiri.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text vikkiri is an aorist 3rd singular of vikkiṇāti, used figuratively for giving away or spending wealth. The form can also be read as an aorist of vikirati (scatters), which fits the meaning 'scattered'.
vikkiri.example_1: Tato paṭṭhāya seṭṭhi asītikoṭidhanaṃ buddhasāsaneyeva vikkiri.
vikkiri.translation_1: From that time on, the rich man scattered 800 million in wealth in the Buddha's dispensation.

āvajjituṃ.meaning_2: to consider; to turn one's attention (to); to reflect (on)
āvajjituṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Infinitive in a prohibitive expression (āvajjituṃ na vaṭṭati). From veṭhati family? Usually analysed as ā + √vaj (go on, turn) = 'turn towards'; alternatively connected with √vaṭṭ.
āvajjituṃ.example_1: Satthā ‘‘ evarūpassa visabhāgajanassa kathitaṃ kathaṃ nāma āvajjituṃ na vaṭṭati, evarūpaṃ asamannāharitvā attano katākatameva oloketuṃ vaṭṭatī ’’ ti vatvā imaṃ gāthamāha –
āvajjituṃ.translation_1: The Teacher said, “It is not right to consider the talk of such an incompatible person; one should not pay attention to such, but should instead reflect on one’s own deeds and misdeeds,” and having said this, he spoke this verse –

cālanaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative noun; 'cālanaṃ nāma ... cālanasadisaṃ' in the text compares unsettling a family to shaking the earth. Neuter nominative singular.
cālanaṃ.example_1: Rājā amaccehi saddhiṃ mantetvā ‘‘ jotikādīnaṃ mahākulānaṃ cālanaṃ nāma mahāpathaviyā cālanasadisaṃ, meṇḍakamahāseṭṭhissa putto dhanañcayaseṭṭhi nāma atthi, tena saddhiṃ mantetvā paṭivacanaṃ te dassāmī ’’ ti vatvā taṃ pakkosāpetvā, tāta, kosalarājā ‘‘‘ ekaṃ dhanaseṭṭhiṃ gahetvā gamissāmī ’ ti vadati, tvaṃ tena saddhiṃ gacchāhī ’’ ti.
cālanaṃ.translation_1: The king consulted with his ministers and said, “Moving such great families like Jotiya’s is like moving the earth. But Dhanañjaya, son of Meṇḍaka, exists. I will consult with him and then give you an answer.” Having sent for the rich man Dhanañjaya, he said: “My friend, the King of Kosala says: ‘I will take a rich man with me.’ You go with him.”

ṭhapitavajirapanti.meaning_2: a row of set diamonds; a string of inlaid diamonds
ṭhapitavajirapanti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound of ṭhapita (set, placed), vajira (diamond) and panti (row, line). In the text it is part of a simile for white, even teeth, and looks nominative singular.
ṭhapitavajirapanti.example_1: Mahāpuññāya hi itthiyā kesā morakalāpasadisā hutvā muñcitvā vissaṭṭhā nivāsanantaṃ paharitvā nivattitvā uddhaggā tiṭṭhanti, idaṃ kesakalyāṇaṃ nāma, dantāvaraṇaṃ bimbaphalasadisaṃ vaṇṇasampannaṃ samaṃ suphusitaṃ hoti, idaṃ maṃsakalyāṇaṃ nāma, dantā sukkā samā aviraḷā ussāpetvā ṭhapitavajirapanti viya samacchinnasaṅkhapanti viya ca sobhanti, idaṃ aṭṭhikalyāṇaṃ nāma, kāḷiyā cuṇṇakādīhi avilitto eva chavivaṇṇo siniddho nīluppaladāmasadiso hoti, odātāya ca kaṇikārapupphadāmasadiso hoti, idaṃ chavikalyāṇaṃ nāma, dasakkhattuṃ vijātāpi kho pana sakiṃ vijātā viya avigatayobbanāyeva hoti, idaṃ vayakalyāṇaṃ nāma hoti.
ṭhapitavajirapanti.translation_1: For a woman of great merit, the hair is like a peacock’s tail; when released, it touches the hem of her skirt and then the ends curl upwards—this is beauty of hair (kesakalyāṇaṃ). Her lips are like a bright red gourd, even in color and soft to the touch—this is beauty of flesh (maṃsakalyāṇaṃ). Her teeth are white, even, and without gaps, shining like a row of set diamonds or a polished conch-shell—this is beauty of bone (aṭṭhikalyāṇaṃ). For a dark-complexioned woman, her skin is smooth and as deep blue as a lotus garland without any cosmetics; for a fair woman, it is like a garland of kanikara flowers—this is beauty of skin (chavikalyāṇaṃ). And even though she has given birth ten times, her youth remains as fresh as if she had only given birth once—this is beauty of youth (vayakalyāṇaṃ).

samacchinnasaṅkhapanti.meaning_2: a row of evenly cut conch shells; a line of conches cut to the same size
samacchinnasaṅkhapanti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Simile describing beautiful teeth in the Dhammapada commentary. In the text the final -i of panti has been elided before 'viya'.
samacchinnasaṅkhapanti.example_1: Mahāpuññāya hi itthiyā kesā morakalāpasadisā hutvā muñcitvā vissaṭṭhā nivāsanantaṃ paharitvā nivattitvā uddhaggā tiṭṭhanti, idaṃ kesakalyāṇaṃ nāma, dantāvaraṇaṃ bimbaphalasadisaṃ vaṇṇasampannaṃ samaṃ suphusitaṃ hoti, idaṃ maṃsakalyāṇaṃ nāma, dantā sukkā samā aviraḷā ussāpetvā ṭhapitavajirapanti viya samacchinnasaṅkhapanti viya ca sobhanti, idaṃ aṭṭhikalyāṇaṃ nāma, kāḷiyā cuṇṇakādīhi avilitto eva chavivaṇṇo siniddho nīluppaladāmasadiso hoti, odātāya ca kaṇikārapupphadāmasadiso hoti, idaṃ chavikalyāṇaṃ nāma, dasakkhattuṃ vijātāpi kho pana sakiṃ vijātā viya avigatayobbanāyeva hoti, idaṃ vayakalyāṇaṃ nāma hoti.
samacchinnasaṅkhapanti.translation_1: For a woman of great merit, the hair is like a peacock’s tail; when released, it touches the hem of her skirt and then the ends curl upwards—this is beauty of hair (kesakalyāṇaṃ). Her lips are like a bright red gourd, even in color and soft to the touch—this is beauty of flesh (maṃsakalyāṇaṃ). Her teeth are white, even, and without gaps, shining like a row of set diamonds or a polished conch-shell—this is beauty of bone (aṭṭhikalyāṇaṃ). For a dark-complexioned woman, her skin is smooth and as deep blue as a lotus garland without any cosmetics; for a fair woman, it is like a garland of kanikara flowers—this is beauty of skin (chavikalyāṇaṃ). And even though she has given birth ten times, her youth remains as fresh as if she had only given birth once—this is beauty of youth (vayakalyāṇaṃ).

makkhāpetvā.meaning_2: having caused to smear; having had (it) anointed
makkhāpetvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative absolutive of makkheti (to smear, anoint); here used of having the mare anointed with oil. Formed from the causative stem makkhāpe- plus -tvā.
makkhāpetvā.example_1: Sā dāsīhi daṇḍadīpikā gāhāpetvā tattha gantvā vaḷavaṃ uṇhodakena nhāpetvā telena makkhāpetvā attano vasanaṭṭhānameva agamāsi.
makkhāpetvā.translation_1: She had her maids carry torches, went to the stable, bathed the mare with warm water, anointed it with oil, and returned to her own quarters.

paṭidenti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 3rd plural present in the text (paṭidenti). The commentary glosses it as returning borrowed goods; the simplex dadāti is the base verb.
paṭidenti.example_1: Taṃ ‘‘ yācitakaṃ upakaraṇaṃ gahetvā ye paṭidenti, tesaññeva dātabban ’’ ti sandhāya vuttaṃ.
paṭidenti.translation_1: was said meaning, ‘One should give only to those who return what they have borrowed.’
paṭidenti.example_2: ‘‘ Ye na denti , tesaṃ na dātabban ’’ti idampi ye yācitakaṃ gahetvā na paṭidenti, tesaṃ na dātabbanti sandhāya vuttaṃ.
paṭidenti.translation_2: ‘One should not give to those who do not give’ was said meaning, ‘One should not give to those who do not return what they have borrowed.’

vīmaṃsitukāmo.meaning_2: wishing to test; wanting to examine
vīmaṃsitukāmo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound of the infinitive vīmaṃsituṃ and kāma. Nominative singular masculine in the text.
vīmaṃsitukāmo.example_1: Rājā ‘‘ visākhā kira pañcannaṃ hatthīnaṃ balaṃ dhāretī ’’ ti sutvā tassā vihāraṃ gantvā dhammaṃ sutvā āgamanavelāya thāmaṃ vīmaṃsitukāmo hatthiṃ vissajjāpesi, so soṇḍaṃ ukkhipitvā visākhābhimukho agamāsi.
vīmaṃsitukāmo.translation_1: The king, hearing that she had the strength of five elephants, resolved to test her on her way back from the monastery, and had an elephant released against her. The elephant, trunk raised, rushed straight toward Visākhā.
vīmaṃsitukāmo.example_2: ‘‘ rājā kira te, ayye, balaṃ vīmaṃsitukāmo hatthiṃ vissajjāpesī ’’ ti vadiṃsu.
vīmaṃsitukāmo.translation_2: They replied, “Noble mistress, the king wants to test your strength and has released an elephant against you.”

paṭipaṇāmesi.meaning_2: pushed back; sent back; made retreat
paṭipaṇāmesi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative of √nam. 3rd singular aorist in the text; the present is paṭipaṇāmeti. PEU analyses the root as namu, and naṃs/nāmayati are also possible.
paṭipaṇāmesi.example_1: Visākhā imaṃ disvā,‘‘ kiṃ palāyitena, kathaṃ nu kho taṃ gaṇhissāmī ’’ ti cintetvā,‘‘ sace taṃ daḷhaṃ gaṇhissāmi, vinasseyyā ’’ ti dvīhi aṅgulīhi soṇḍāya gahetvā paṭipaṇāmesi.
paṭipaṇāmesi.translation_1: Visākhā thought, “What is the use of running? How shall I handle it? If I grab it too firmly, I might destroy it.” So, holding its trunk between two fingers, she pushed it back.

gaṇhiṃtu.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text has gaṇhiṃtu, an unusual form; it may be a variant of gaṇhantu (3rd plural imperative) or of gaṇhituṃ (infinitive), possibly misspelt. Meaning 'to buy' fits the sentence.
gaṇhiṃtu.example_1: Bhattakaṃ dhanaṃ datvā gaṇhiṃtu na koci sakkhissati.
gaṇhiṃtu.translation_1: No one would be able to buy it, having paid the necessary wealth.

pilandhituṃ.meaning_2: to wear; to put on; to adorn oneself (with)
pilandhituṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Infinitive of pilandhati. Used with ornaments and flowers in the text (pilandhituṃ ... pasādhanaṃ, sumanapupphāni pilandhituṃ). The PEU splits it as piḷandha + tuṃ; the form in the text has the common single-l spelling.
pilandhituṃ.example_1: Tasmā visākhā sayameva tassa mūlaṃ datvā satasahassādhikā nava koṭiyo sakaṭe āropetvā vihāraṃ netvā satthāraṃ vanditvā,‘‘ bhante, mayhaṃ ayyena ānandattherena mama pasādhanaṃ hatthena āmaṭṭhaṃ, tena āmaṭṭhakālato paṭṭhāya na sakkā taṃ mayā pilandhituṃ.
pilandhituṃ.translation_1: Therefore, Visākhā herself paid the price and, taking the ornament worth over nine crores plus one hundred thousand for the workmanship, went to the monastery and worshipped the Teacher, saying: “Venerable sir, my noble master, Elder Ānanda, has touched my ornament with his hand, and I cannot wear it since then.
pilandhituṃ.example_2: So pubbe coraghātakakammaṃ karonto ‘‘ ahatasāṭake nivāsetuṃ, navasappinā saṅkhataṃ khīrayāguṃ pivituṃ, sumanapupphāni pilandhituṃ, gandhe vilimpitun ’’ ti imāni cattāri na labhi.
pilandhituṃ.translation_2: Previously, while performing the executioner's work, he could not obtain these four things: wearing fresh, unsoiled clothes, drinking milk-porridge made with new ghee, wearing jasmine flowers, and anointing himself with perfumes.

vallatā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Abstract noun of vallabha (dear, beloved), equivalent to vallabhabhāva in the same sentence. Nominative singular, subject of hoti.
vallatā.example_1: Sā tassā satthārā saddhiṃ vissāsena kathanañca vallabhabhāvañca disvā,‘ kiṃ nu kho katvā evaṃ buddhānaṃ vallatā hotī ’ ti cintetvā satthāraṃ pucchi –
vallatā.translation_1: Seeing her intimacy and familiarity with the Buddha, she thought, ‘By doing what does one become so intimate with the Buddhas?’ and asked the Buddha –

paricchattakarukkho.meaning_2: Pāricchattaka tree; coral tree of Tāvatiṃsa heaven
paricchattakarukkho.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Nominative singular in the text. The Pāricchattaka (coral) tree in Tāvatiṃsa heaven; -rukkha is the compound member here, written with single k after the preceding vowel.
paricchattakarukkho.example_1: Tattha na pupphagandhoti tāvatiṃsabhavane paricchattakarukkho āyāmato ca vitthārato ca yojanasatiko, tassa pupphānaṃ ābhā paññāsa yojanāni gacchati, gandho yojanasataṃ, sopi anuvātameva gacchati, paṭivātaṃ pana aṭṭhaṅgulamattampi gantuṃ na sakkoti, evarūpopi na pupphagandho paṭivātameti.
paricchattakarukkho.translation_1: Therein, the scent of flowers does not means: in the Tāvatiṃsa heaven, the Pāricchattaka tree is a hundred yojanas in length and width. The radiance of its flowers extends for fifty yojanas, and its fragrance for a hundred yojanas. Yet that fragrance goes only with the wind; it cannot go even half a finger’s breadth against the wind. Even such a flower fragrance does not go against the wind.

otaggasarīro.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Bahutīhi kammāya: 'otagga' (bent) + 'sarīra' (body). Nominative singular used in the text to describe Sakka's aged form.
otaggasarīro.example_1: Sakko ‘‘ tumhādisiyo therassa piṇḍapātaṃ kiṃ dassantī ’’ ti sayaṃ dātukāmo hutvā, jarājiṇṇo mahallako khaṇḍadanto palitakeso otaggasarīro mahallakatanta vāyo hutvā sujampi devadhītaraṃ tathārūpameva mahallikaṃ katvā ekaṃ pesakāravīthiṃ māpetvā tantaṃ pasārento acchi.
otaggasarīro.translation_1: Sakka thought, “How could you possibly give alms to the Elder?” Wishing to give them himself, he transformed into an old weaver, decrepit with age, broken teeth, gray hair, and a bent back. He made the goddess Sujā into a similar old woman, manifested a weavers’ lane, and sat there spinning thread.

pāthetvā.meaning_2: has (them) beaten; has (them) struck; makes (them) suffer
pāthetvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive of a causative verb; the text has pāthetvā = pāthe + tvā, 'having had (them) beaten'. The simplex √path means 'go, move'; the causative sense 'cause to go (with sticks), beat' fits the context. The PEU entry pātheyya is probably unrelated.
pāthetvā.example_1: Sirigutto tesu patitesu dvāraṃ pidahitvā te uttiṇṇuttiṇṇe ‘‘ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṃ kasmā na jānāthā ’’ ti daṇḍehi pāthetvā ‘‘ ettakaṃ etesaṃ vaṭṭissatī ’’ ti dvāraṃ vivarāpesi.
pāthetvā.translation_1: After they fell, Sirigutta closed the door. As they crawled out, he had them beaten with sticks, saying: “Why did you not know the past, future, and present?” Finally, saying this was sufficient punishment, he had the door opened.

pothāpetvā.meaning_2: having caused to be beaten; having had (someone) beaten; having ordered a beating
pothāpetvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative absolutive; the text uses it for having someone beaten (or beaten and tortured).
pothāpetvā.example_1: Te tattha asaṇṭhahitvā patite patite puna pothāpetvā ‘‘ alaṃ ettakaṃ tumhākan ’’ ti uyyojesi.
pothāpetvā.translation_1: Unable to stand, they fell again and again, and he had them beaten once more, saying: “This much is enough for you,” and let them go.
pothāpetvā.example_2: Garahadinno taṃ vippakāraṃ disvā kuddho ‘‘ nāsitamhi siriguttena, hatthaṃ pasāretvā vandantānaṃ sadevake loke yathāruciyā dātuṃ samatthe nāma puññakkhettabhūte mama, ayye, pothāpetvā byasanaṃ pāpesī ’’ ti rājakulaṃ gantvā tassa kahāpaṇasahassaṃ daṇḍaṃ kāresi.
pothāpetvā.translation_2: Garahadinna, seeing this disaster, was angry and said: “Sirigutta has ruined me! He has beaten my noble ones, who are a field of merit, who can bestow the six celestial worlds on those who worship them with outstretched hands, and he has brought humiliation upon them.” He went to the royal court and had a fine of a thousand coins inflicted on Sirigutta.

dhamāpetvā.meaning_2: having caused to blow; having had (the fire) blown
dhamāpetvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative absolutive of dhamati (to blow) with the *āpe sign; here of blowing a fire all night.
dhamāpetvā.example_1: Garahadinno ‘‘ idānissa kattabbayuttakaṃ jānissāmī ’’ ti dvinnaṃ gehānaṃ antare mahantaṃ āvāṭaṃ khaṇāpetvā asītisakaṭamattāni khadiradārūni āharāpetvā pūrāpetvā aggiṃ datvā khadiraṅgārarāsīnaṃ yojāpetvā sabbarattiṃ dhamāpetvā khadiraṅgārarāsiṃ kārāpetvā āvāṭamatthake rukkhapadarāni ṭhapāpetvā kilañjena paṭicchādetvā gomayena limpāpetvā ekena passena dubbaladaṇḍake attharitvā gamanamaggaṃ kāresi,‘‘ evaṃ akkantaakkantakāle daṇḍakesu bhaggesu parivaṭṭetvā aṅgārakāsuyaṃ patissantī ’’ ti maññamāno gehapacchābhāge siriguttena ṭhapitaniyāmeneva cāṭiyo ṭhapāpesi, āsanānipi tatheva paññāpesi.
dhamāpetvā.translation_1: Garahadinna thought, “Now I shall know what ought to be done to that ascetic Gotama.” He had a large pit dug between the two houses, brought eighty cartloads of acacia wood, lit a fire, had it blown all night long, and created a pit of blazing charcoal. He placed logs over the pit, covered them with matting, smeared them with cow dung, laid down weak sticks on one side, and created a walkway, thinking, “When they step there, the sticks will break, they will fall into the charcoal pit, and they will be crushed.” He had the vessels placed behind the house in the same way Sirigutta had done, and had seats prepared likewise.

pothiyamāno.meaning_2: being beaten; being pelted; being struck
pothiyamāno.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Present participle passive of pothīyati (to be beaten); the text gives pothiyamāno, nominative singular masculine. The PEU analysis putha + ya + māna is likely a misreading.
pothiyamāno.example_1: Ussāraṇāya vattamānāya leḍḍudaṇḍādīhi pothiyamāno mahājano palāyanto gīvaṃ parivaṭṭetvāpi oloketiyeva.
pothiyamāno.translation_1: As the crowds were cleared away, pelted by clods of earth and beaten with sticks, they ran here and there, craning their necks to look back.

ghātāpetvā.meaning_2: having caused to be killed; having had (someone) killed
ghātāpetvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative of √han with the -tvā absolutive ending; the form comes from a sandhi of quotation. The absolutive describes an action completed before the main verb in the quoted sentence.
ghātāpetvā.example_1: ‘‘ vibhātakkhaṇeyeva taṃ purisaṃ ghātāpetvā taṃ itthiṃ ānessāmī ’’ ti.
ghātāpetvā.translation_1: “At the very moment it becomes light, I will have that man killed and bring that woman here.”

nimīletuṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Infinitive nimīletuṃ in the text, 'to close (the eyes)'. Causative of nimīlati; the simplex √mīl with the -e causative sign.
nimīletuṃ.example_1: Rājā niddaṃ alabhanto majjhimayāmasamanantare taṃ saddaṃ sutvā bhīto utrastamānaso ‘‘ kiṃ nu kho mayhaṃ jīvitantarāyo bhavissati, udāhu me aggamahesiyā, udāhu me rajjaṃ vinassissatī ’’ ti cintento sakalarattiṃ akkhīni nimīletuṃ nāsakkhi.
nimīletuṃ.translation_1: The king, unable to sleep, heard that sound right after the middle watch. Terrified and with an anxious mind, he thought, “Will my life end, or that of my chief queen, or will my kingdom be destroyed?” and he was unable to close his eyes for the rest of the night.

soitīti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] soitīti = soti + iti; the -ti is the quotative particle. The alternative reading is hoti from √hū, but the -oi- spelling suggests soti.

āvīkarontā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Nominative plural masculine of the present participle of āvīkaroti, agreeing with pāpakammino; the text has the sandhi form āvīkarontā before evamāhaṃsu.
āvīkarontā.example_1: ‘‘ mā bhāyi, mahārāja, tava antarāyo natthi, pāpakammino satthā attano dukkhaṃ āvīkarontā evamāhaṃsū ’’ ti.
āvīkarontā.translation_1: “Do not be afraid, Great King; there is no danger for you. Those wrongdoers spoke thus, manifesting their own suffering.”

maṅkuṇasaṅghassa.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Genitive singular in the text (maṅkuṇasaṅghassa), dependent on bhattaṃ katvā: 'having become food for a swarm of bedbugs'. Slight doubt about the spelling and exact meaning of maṅkuṇa.
maṅkuṇasaṅghassa.example_1: Tassā dīghabhāvaṃ attānaṃ maṅkuṇasaṅghassa bhattaṃ katvā yāva sūriyuggamanā samparivattakaṃ semāno mahākusītopi, subhojanaṃ bhuñjitvā sirisayane sayamāno kāmabhogīpi na jānāti, sabbarattiṃ pana padhānaṃ padahanto yogāvacaro ca, dhammakathaṃ kathento dhammakathiko ca, āsanasamīpe ṭhatvā dhammaṃ suṇanto ca, sīsarogādiphuṭṭho vā hatthapādacchedanādiṃ patto vā vedanābhibhūto ca, rattiṃ maggapaṭipanno addhiko ca jānāti.
maṅkuṇasaṅghassa.translation_1: A very lazy person, who lies tossing and turning until sunrise while being eaten by a swarm of bedbugs, or a sensualist who, having enjoyed fine food, sleeps on a royal couch, does not know the length of the night. However, a meditator engaged in mental development all night, a Dhamma speaker teaching all night, a listener sitting near the seat all night, someone suffering from a headache or other illness, or one afflicted by pain such as the cutting of hands and feet, as well as a traveler walking through the night—they know it.

paccisaṃ.meaning_2: in return; correspondingly; according to (the number of)
paccisaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Possibly pati + isaṃ, an adverbial form meaning 'in return, correspondingly'; verse, meaning uncertain.
paccisaṃ.translation_1: “Having cut off the head of one, I suffered according to the number of hairs;

siṅgilasakuṇo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Nominative singular in the text. Name of a bird (Ploceus philippinus, the baya weaver) famous for its hanging nest; in the story it is identified with Kassapa.
siṅgilasakuṇo.example_1: Atīte bārāṇasiyaṃ brahmadatte rajjaṃ kārente himavantapadese eko siṅgilasakuṇo kulāvakaṃ katvā vasi.
siṅgilasakuṇo.translation_1: In the past, when Brahmadatta was reigning in Bārāṇasī, a certain singila bird made a nest and lived in the Himavanta region.
siṅgilasakuṇo.example_2: ‘‘ tadā makkaṭo kuṭidūsakabhikkhu ahosi, siṅgilasakuṇo kassapo ahosī ’’ ti.
siṅgilasakuṇo.translation_2: “At that time, the monkey was the hut-destroying bhikkhu, the singila bird was Kassapa.”

siṅgilo.meaning_2: baya weaver bird; weaver bird (Ploceus philippinus)
siṅgilo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Name of a bird (baya weaver) in the Dhammapada commentary. Nominative singular in the text, the subject of gāthamāha. PEU suggests siṅga + ila but the derivation is uncertain.
siṅgilo.translation_1: The singila bird saw him and said a verse —
siṅgilo.example_2: Atha naṃ ‘‘ evarūpassa tava kathaṃ gharāvāso ijjhissatī ’’ ti garahanto siṅgilo imaṃ gāthādvayamāha –
siṅgilo.translation_2: Then, censuring him, thinking, “How could a household life succeed for one like you?” the singila bird spoke these two verses —

sīliyaṃ.meaning_2: virtuousness; good conduct; moral habit; (or) base habits
sīliyaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular. In the verse vītivattassu sīliyaṃ the sense is likely 'overcome (your) habits/conduct', so the word may carry the meaning 'habit; behaviour' rather than 'virtue'; the PEU gloss takes it as 'a virtuous, discerning person' (nt), which is doubtful.
sīliyaṃ.translation_1: “You should exert your power, you should overcome your base habits;

saṃbhogaparibhogaṃ.meaning_2: shared consumption and enjoyment; communal use and enjoyment
saṃbhogaparibhogaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text, object of karonto. Dvandva compound; saṃbhoga is sharing, paribhoga is using/enjoying.
saṃbhogaparibhogaṃ.example_1: Ekacariyanti etesu hi seyyaṃ labhamāno sīlādīhi vaḍḍhati, sadisaṃ labhamāno na parihāyati, hīnena pana saddhiṃ ekato vasanto ekato saṃbhogaparibhogaṃ karonto sīlādīhi parihāyati.
saṃbhogaparibhogaṃ.translation_1: ‘Resolutely travel alone’ means: among these, one who finds someone superior grows in virtues such as morality; one who finds someone equal does not decline; but one who lives together with someone inferior, engaging in shared consumption and activities, declines in virtues such as morality.

uppaṇḍayamāno.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Present participle of uppaṇḍayati (causative of paṇḍ, 'mock'), agreeing with sahāyakacoro; nominative singular here. In the text it takes the accusative naṃ as its object.
uppaṇḍayamāno.example_1: Atha naṃ sahāyakacoro attano bhariyāya saddhiṃ uppaṇḍayamāno ‘‘ tvaṃ atipaṇḍitatāya attano gehe pākabhattamūlampi na nipphādesī ’’ ti āha.
uppaṇḍayamāno.translation_1: Then, mocking him along with his own wife, the thief-companion said, “Because you are excessively wise, you cannot even generate the cost of a meal in your own house.”

mahātuṇḍilassa.meaning_2: Great Boar; name of the boar in the Tuṇḍila birth story
mahātuṇḍilassa.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Name of the boar who taught the Dhamma in the Tuṇḍila Jātaka. Genitive singular in the text, depending on dhammadesanaṃ.
mahātuṇḍilassa.example_1: Satthā taṃ sutvā ‘‘ na, bhikkhave, idāneva, pubbepi ime tiṃsamattā sahāyakā dhuttā hutvā tuṇḍilajātake (jā.1.6.88 ādayo) mahātuṇḍilassa dhammadesanaṃ sutvāpi khippameva dhammaṃ viññāya pañca sīlāni samādiyiṃsu, te teneva upanissayena etarahi nisinnāsaneyeva arahattaṃ pattā ’’ ti vatvā dhammaṃ desento imaṃ gāthamāha –
mahātuṇḍilassa.translation_1: Upon hearing this, the Teacher said, “Monks, this is not the first time; in the past, too, these thirty companions were roguish, and hearing the Dhamma teaching of the great boar in the Tuṇḍila birth story, they understood the Dhamma quickly and undertook the five precepts. It was because of that same supporting condition that they have attained arahantship just now in their very seats,” and he spoke this verse:

ogāhituṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Infinitive of ogāhati. In the text it depends on avisahanto: 'not daring to enter (the midst of the assembly)'. The PEU entry gives ava+gaha(gāha) and the sense 'to enter'.
ogāhituṃ.example_1: Tadā hi suppabuddhakuṭṭhi parisapariyante nisinno bhagavato dhammadesanaṃ sutvā sotāpattiphalaṃ patvā attanā paṭiladdhaguṇaṃ satthu ārocetukāmo parisamajjhe ogāhituṃ avisahanto mahājanassa satthāraṃ vanditvā anugantvā nivattanakāle vihāraṃ agamāsi.
ogāhituṃ.translation_1: At that time, Suppabuddha the leper, seated on the edge of the assembly, heard the Blessed One’s Dhamma teaching, attained the fruit of stream-entry, and, desiring to report the attained quality to the Teacher but not daring to enter the midst of the assembly, waited until the great multitude had worshipped the Teacher and departed, then went to the monastery.

tāḷiyamāno.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Passive present participle of tāḷeti. Nominative singular masculine referring to the man being struck with whips in the sentence.
tāḷiyamāno.example_1: So kasāhi tāḷiyamāno aññaṃ kiñci avatvā ‘‘ passānanda, āsīvisoti, passāmi bhagavā ghoraviso ’’ ti vadanto gacchati.
tāḷiyamāno.translation_1: As he was struck with whips, he said nothing else but, “Look, Ānanda, a poisonous snake! I see, Blessed One, a deadly poisonous snake!” and kept walking.

upariṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Form of upari used before a noun in the text: aṃsakūṭānaṃ upariṃ (over the shoulders).
upariṃ.example_1: Pabbājentā ca pana galappamāṇe āvāṭe ṭhapetvā dvinnaṃ aṃsakūṭānaṃ upariṃ padarāni datvā tesaṃ upari nisīditvā tālaṭṭhikhaṇḍena kese luñciṃsu.
upariṃ.translation_1: While initiating him, they placed him in a pit up to his neck, placed boards over his shoulders, and sitting on the boards, pulled out his hair with palmyra combs.

lābukaṃ.meaning_2: water-gourd; calabash gourd; small gourd bottle
lābukaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text, listed among an ascetic's belongings. The PEU entry marks it neuter; some sources treat lābu as feminine.
lābukaṃ.example_1: ‘‘ Sace tvaṃ pabbajito, kahaṃ te lābukaṃ, kahaṃ dhūmakaṭacchuko, kahaṃ yaññasuttakan ’’ ti?
lābukaṃ.translation_1: “If you are an ascetic, where is your water-gourd, your fire-stirring spoon, your sacrificial thread?”

kukkuccāyitvā.meaning_2: having been scrupulous (about); having had remorse (about); having hesitated (over)
kukkuccāyitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in -tvā of a denominative verb from kukkucca. Used with kālaṃ and bhattaṃ in the sense of being anxious/scrupulous about time or food. PEU splits it as kukkucca + aya + tvā; root connection is doubtful.
kukkuccāyitvā.example_1: ‘‘ ayaṃ ettakaṃ kālaṃ tumhehi ābhataṃ sakkāraṃ kusaggena jivhagge ṭhapetvā ‘ tapacaraṇaṃ pūremī ’ ti idha nivuṭṭho, sacepi iminā upāyena vassasataṃ tapacaraṇaṃ pūreyya, yā cassa idāni kālaṃ vā bhattaṃ vā kukkuccāyitvā abhuñjantassa bhattacchedanakusalacetanā, tassā taṃ tapacaraṇaṃ soḷasiṃ kalampi na agghatī ’’ ti anusandhiṃ ghaṭetvā dhammaṃ desento imaṃ gāthamāha –
kukkuccāyitvā.translation_1: “Having placed the offerings brought by you on the tip of his tongue with the tip of a blade of kusa grass, saying, ‘I am fulfilling my ascetic practice,’ he has dwelt here all this time. Even if he were to fulfill this ascetic practice for a hundred years in this way, it would not be worth a sixteenth part of the wholesome intention of that person who now, out of remorse, abstains from taking food,” and linking the connection, he taught the Dhamma by speaking this verse:
kukkuccāyitvā.example_2: Ayaṃ panettha attho – yā cassa tathā tapacaraṇaṃ pūrentassa vassasataṃ cetanā yā ca saṅkhātadhammānaṃ kālaṃ vā bhattaṃ vā kukkuccāyitvā abhuñjantānaṃ ekā bhattacchedanakusalacetanā, tassā cetanāya sā tāva dīgharattaṃ pavattacetanā soḷasiṃ kalaṃ na agghati.
kukkuccāyitvā.translation_2: Herein, the meaning is this: Whatever intention a fool has while fulfilling such ascetic practices for a hundred years, and whatever wholesome intention of abstaining from food those who have realized the Dhamma have, when they abstain from food out of remorse regarding the time or the meal—that sustained intention of theirs is not worth a sixteenth part of that intention.

sāḷittakasippe.meaning_2: art of stone-throwing; skill of throwing small stones
sāḷittakasippe.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative singular in the text: "in the art of stone-throwing". The first member sāḷittaka is obscure; the PEU glosses it as "small stone".
sāḷittakasippe.example_1: Atīte kira bārāṇasiyaṃ sāḷittakasippe nipphattiṃ patto eko pīṭhasappi ahosi.
sāḷittakasippe.translation_1: In the past, they say, there lived in Bārāṇasī a cripple who had attained perfection in the art of stone-throwing.

maṅguubhāvaṃ.meaning_2: state of being speechless; embarrassment; inability to speak; state of confusion
maṅguubhāvaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text (āpajjitvā = having fallen into). The reading maṅguubhāvaṃ is probably for maṅkubhāvaṃ (maṅku + bhāva), 'speechless embarrassment'. No verbal root; compound of an adjective of uncertain form plus bhāva.
maṅguubhāvaṃ.example_1: Brāhmaṇo maṅguubhāvaṃ āpajjitvā tato paṭṭhāya mukhaṃ vivaritvā raññā saddhiṃ sallapituṃ nasakkhi.
maṅguubhāvaṃ.translation_1: The priest was embarrassed, and from then on, he could not open his mouth to converse with the king.

vipātentaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Present participle (masculine accusative singular here) agreeing with muddhaṃ; formed from the causative vipāteti. The PEU entry points to vipātayanta, a variant of the same participle.
vipātentaṃ.example_1: Tassa hi taṃ sukkaṃsaṃ hanantaṃ paññāsaṅkhātaṃ muddhaṃ vipātentaṃ viddhaṃsentameva hantīti.
vipātentaṃ.translation_1: For while destroying his portion of merit, it destroys—that is, ruins—his wisdom, which is what is meant by 'head'.

khuṃsitoti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text reads khuṃsitoti = khuṃsito + iti, a quotation of the past participle khuṃsita used in direct speech; this entry is for the underlying verb. The PEU entry khuṃsita (khusi + ta) is presumably a mis-split of the same word.

paṭikhamāpito.meaning_2: caused to forgive; caused to pardon; made to excuse
paṭikhamāpito.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative past participle used passively in the text: 'he was made to pardon (by the layman)'. Nominative singular.
paṭikhamāpito.example_1: So upāsakena ‘‘ khamāmahaṃ, bhante, sace mayhaṃ doso atthi, khamatha me ’’ ti paṭikhamāpito satthārā dinne ovāde ṭhatvā katipāheneva saha paṭisambhidāhi arahattaṃ pāpuṇi.
paṭikhamāpito.translation_1: He was pardoned by the upāsaka, who said, “Venerable sir, I pardon you; if there is any fault of mine, please pardon me.” He then stood by the Teacher’s admonition and within a few days attained Arahantship together with the analytic knowledges.

accuṇhaatisītaatiambilādiparibhogaṃ.meaning_2: consumption of very hot, very cold, and very sour foods
accuṇhaatisītaatiambilādiparibhogaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text, object of vajjetvā. A long compound describing the foods avoided by the pregnant woman.
accuṇhaatisītaatiambilādiparibhogaṃ.example_1: Tassā accuṇhaatisītaatiambilādiparibhogaṃ vajjetvā sukhena gabbhaṃ parihariyamānāya evarūpo dohaḷo uppajji ‘‘ aho vatāhaṃ sāriputtattherappamukhāni pañca bhikkhusatāni nimantetvā gehe nisīdāpetvā asambhinnakhīrapāyasaṃ datvā sayampi kāsāyavatthāni paridahitvā suvaṇṇasarakaṃ ādāya āsanapariyante nisīditvā ettakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ ucchiṭṭhapāyasaṃ paribhuñjeyyan ’’ ti.
accuṇhaatisītaatiambilādiparibhogaṃ.translation_1: While she was carrying the child in comfort, avoiding hot, cold, and sour foods, this pregnancy craving arose: “Oh, if only I could invite five hundred bhikkhus headed by the Elder Sāriputta, seat them in my house, serve them unmixed milk-rice porridge, and while I myself am robed in ocher garments and holding a gold bowl, could sit at the end of the seat and consume the left-over porridge of those bhikkhus.”

apakaḍḍhitvā.meaning_2: having withdrawn; having pulled away; having removed
apakaḍḍhitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in -itvā from apakaḍḍhati (apa + √kaḍḍh). In the sentence it describes the finger being pulled back from the blanket before it is dropped at the Elder's feet.
apakaḍḍhitvā.example_1: So theraṃ vandanakāle kambalato aṅguliṃ apakaḍḍhitvā kambalaṃ therassa pādamūle pātesi.
apakaḍḍhitvā.translation_1: When worshipping the Elder, he withdrew his finger from the blanket and dropped it at the Elder’s feet.

konāmoti.meaning_2: what name?; what is (his) name?; who?
konāmoti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Iti added in text; the entry is for the main word. Compound of the interrogative pronoun ka and nāma; used to ask a person's name.

lābhūpanissā.meaning_2: support for gain; basis for acquisition; path to worldly gains
lābhūpanissā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound of lābha and upanissā. Nominative singular in the text, where it names an unrighteous means of obtaining gains.
lābhūpanissā.translation_1: This is called the unrighteous path to worldly gains.

kujjhitabbaṃ.meaning_2: to be angry (with); one should be angry; fit to be angry with
kujjhitabbaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Gerundive in -tabba from kujjhati; negated na kujjhitabbaṃ in the text, nominative singular neuter used impersonally: 'one should not be angry'.
kujjhitabbaṃ.example_1: Tadā kira vaḍḍhakīhi pādassa arogakaraṇabhāvena kahaṃ attano upakāraṃ ñatvā sabbasetassa hatthipotakassa dāyako ekacāriko hatthī sāriputtatthero ahosīti evaṃ theraṃ ārabbha jātakaṃ kathetvā rādhattheraṃ ārabbha,‘‘ bhikkhave, bhikkhunā nāma rādhena viya suvacena bhavitabbaṃ, dosaṃ dassetvā ovadiyamānenapi na kujjhitabbaṃ, ovādadāyako pana nidhiācikkhaṇako viya daṭṭhabbo ’’ ti vatvā anusandhiṃ ghaṭetvā dhammaṃ desento imaṃ gāthamāha –
kujjhitabbaṃ.translation_1: Then, knowing the service rendered to him by the carpenters by healing his foot, the solitary elephant that gave a pure white baby elephant to the carpenters was the Elder Sāriputta. Having told this Jātaka concerning the Elder, and referring to the Elder Rādha, he said, “Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu should be easy to correct like Rādha; even when being admonished and having a fault pointed out, he should not be angry. Rather, one who gives instruction should be seen as one pointing out a hidden treasure.” Having said this, establishing the connection, and teaching the Dhamma, he recited this verse—

animantetvāva.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The sandhi -vāva is animantetvā + eva; the entry is for the absolutive animantetvā. Used in both sentences with eva, meaning 'without inviting at all'.
animantetvāva.example_1: So ‘‘ paccekabuddhā kira āgatā ’’ ti sutvā tasmiṃ khaṇe nikkhamitvā āgatakāraṇaṃ pucchitvā ‘‘ ajja, bhante, okāso natthi, sve amhākaṃ vappamaṅgalaṃ, tatiyadivase karissāmī ’’ ti vatvā paccekabuddhe animantetvāva pāvisi.
animantetvāva.translation_1: When the king heard that “Paccekabuddhas have arrived,” he went out, inquired about the reason for their coming, and said, “Venerable sirs, there is no opportunity today, for tomorrow is our plowing festival; I will do it on the third day,” and without inviting the Paccekabuddhas, he entered his palace.
animantetvāva.example_2: Rājāpi ‘‘ mayhaṃ putto mama gehaṃ anāgantvā kahaṃ gamissatī ’’ ti animantetvāva agamāsi.
animantetvāva.translation_2: Even the king, thinking, “If my son does not come to my house, where will he go?” departed without inviting him.

idañcidañcāti.meaning_2: “this and that!”; “such and such!”; thinking “this and that”
idañcidañcāti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Quotation of vague speech: idaṃ ca idaṃ ca iti, 'this and that' (cf. iti in the sense of a quoted thought or utterance). In the text it precedes itarānipi dve sāsanāni ārocayiṃsu.
idañcidañcāti.example_1: Te idañcidañcāti itarānipi dve sāsanāni ārocayiṃsu.
idañcidañcāti.translation_1: They informed her of the other two messages, saying, “This and that.”

sappikaroṭikañceva.meaning_2: a ghee jar and; a pot of ghee too
sappikaroṭikañceva.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of sappikaroṭikaṃ (nom sg of sappikaroṭika, 'ghee jar', nt) + ceva. In the sentence it is the first item of a list of things given by the merchant's wife, coordinated with dadhibhājanaṃ by ca … ca. Variant spelling sappikaroṭikaṃ ceva.
sappikaroṭikañceva.example_1: Seṭṭhibhariyāpi puna tassā ekaṃ sappikaroṭikañceva dadhibhājanañca kaṭukabhaṇḍañca suddhataṇḍuḷināḷiñca dāpesi.
sappikaroṭikañceva.translation_1: The merchant’s wife also gave her a vessel of ghee, a vessel of curds, hot spices, and a measure of clean rice.

suddhataṇḍuḷināḷiñca.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Text has suddhataṇḍuḷināḷiñca = suddhataṇḍulināḷiṃ + ca; accusative singular. The compound may be read as suddha (clean) + taṇḍuli (rice) + nāḷi (a measure).
suddhataṇḍuḷināḷiñca.example_1: Seṭṭhibhariyāpi puna tassā ekaṃ sappikaroṭikañceva dadhibhājanañca kaṭukabhaṇḍañca suddhataṇḍuḷināḷiñca dāpesi.
suddhataṇḍuḷināḷiñca.translation_1: The merchant’s wife also gave her a vessel of ghee, a vessel of curds, hot spices, and a measure of clean rice.

parittāso.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Nominative singular in the text. Possibly a doublet of paritāsa; the -tt- may reflect assimilation.
parittāso.example_1: Bhikkhūnaṃ ekadivasampi piṇḍapātaṃ ārabbha parittāso nāhosi, icchācāraṃ vajjetvā eva vihariṃsu.
parittāso.translation_1: The bhikkhus were not anxious about almsfood even for a single day, and lived entirely free from desire.

volodakanti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Form is uncertain (variant reading?); occurs with -ti, which is likely the quotation particle (volodakaṃ iti), so the entry is made for the bare word. Not a standard DPD headword; needs verification.

vaṭṭaddhāti.meaning_2: journey of the round of rebirths; journey of saṃsāra
vaṭṭaddhāti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A compound of vaṭṭa (round of rebirths) and addha (journey). In the text it is followed by -ti and is part of a coordinated pair (kantāraddhā vaṭṭaddhā) explaining the two kinds of addhā.
vaṭṭaddhāti.example_1: Tattha gataddhinoti gatamaggassa kantāraddhā vaṭṭaddhāti dve addhā nāma.
vaṭṭaddhāti.translation_1: Therein, gataddhino refers to one who has completed the journey; there are two kinds of ‘journey’: the journey of the wilderness and the journey of the round of rebirths.

māpamādakandarato.meaning_2: from the Māpamāda ravine; from the ravine called Māpamāda
māpamādakandarato.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of mā + apamādakandarato, ablative singular of apamādakandara. Appears in a quotation promising not to go beyond the ravine called Māpamāda.
māpamādakandarato.example_1: Sacepi gaccheyya, māpamādakandarato paraṃ na gamissatī ’’ ti.
māpamādakandarato.translation_1: Even if he were to go, he would not go beyond the Māpamāda Ravine.”

māpamādakandaranti.meaning_2: do not be negligent; do not let a moment pass
māpamādakandaranti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Probably mā + apamādaṃ karonti (or kandaranti); the split is uncertain because no sentence is given. Registered as sandhi.

aṭṭiyanañca.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text joined with -ca as aṭṭiyanañca, part of the phrase attano kāyena aṭṭiyanaṃ, 'disgust with one's own body'.
aṭṭiyanañca.example_1: Thero ‘‘ nāyaṃ bhikkhu mayā pahaṭo ’’ ti avatvāva attano guṇakathaṃ kathento ‘‘ yassa nūna, bhante, kāye kāyagatāsati anupaṭṭhitā assa, so idha aññataraṃ sabrahmacāriṃ āsajja appaṭinissajja cārikaṃ pakkameyyā ’’ ti vatvā ‘‘ seyyathāpi, bhante, pathaviyaṃ sucimpi nikkhipanti, asucimpi nikkhipantī ’’ tiādinā nayena attano pathavīsamacittatañca āpotejovāyo rajoharaṇacaṇḍālakumārakausabhachinnavisāṇasamacittatañca ahikuṇapādīhi viya attano kāyena aṭṭiyanañca medakathālikā viya attano kāyapariharaṇañca pakāsesi.
aṭṭiyanañca.translation_1: Instead of just saying, ‘I did not strike this bhikkhu,’ the Elder, wishing to state his virtues, said, ‘Venerable Sir, if a bhikkhu has not established mindfulness of the body (kāyagatāsati) in his body, he might indeed depart on a tour having offended a fellow celibate in this religion without asking for pardon.’ Then, using similes such as, ‘Just as one throws what is clean and what is unclean onto the earth,’ he revealed his mind to be like the earth, like water, fire, wind, a dust-cloth, a Caṇḍāla youth, an ox with broken horns; he revealed that he knew his body to be like a snake’s corpse and that he maintained his body like a grease-pot.

laddhupasampado.meaning_2: who has received higher ordination; who has obtained the upasampadā
laddhupasampado.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Bahubbīhi compound. Nominative singular masculine ending -o in the text.
laddhupasampado.example_1: Eko kira kosambivāsī kulaputto satthu sāsane pabbajitvā laddhupasampado ‘‘ kosambivāsītissatthero ’’ ti paññāyi.
laddhupasampado.translation_1: They say that a certain youth of standing, residing at Kosambī, went forth in the Teacher’s Dispensation and, having attained higher ordination, became known as Elder Kosambivāsī Tissa.

nevettha.meaning_2: there is no fault here; not here
nevettha.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of na (no) + eva (indeed) + ettha (here), resolving to 'na ... eva ettha' or 'na ettha eva'. Used in the phrase nevettha tumhākaṃ doso atthi meaning 'there is no fault here for you'.
nevettha.example_1: ‘‘ nāhaṃ, bhante, etadatthāya kathesiṃ, tumhākaṃ cittaṃ anurakkhantena mayā evaṃ vuttaṃ nevettha tumhākaṃ doso atthi, na mayhaṃ.
nevettha.translation_1: “Venerable sir, I did not speak for that purpose. It was because I wished to protect your mind that I said this. There is no fault here for you, nor for me.
nevettha.example_2: ‘‘ evaṃ, bhante, mayā khamāpiyamāno maṃ evaṃ vadesi ‘ nevettha tumhākaṃ doso atthi, na mayhaṃ.
nevettha.translation_2: “In this way, venerable sir, when I asked him for forgiveness, he said to me, ‘There is no fault here for you, nor for me.

paṭisammodanaṃ.meaning_2: friendly greeting; exchange of greetings; courteous welcome
paṭisammodanaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text, object of katvā in the idiom paṭisammodanaṃ karoti (exchange friendly greetings).
paṭisammodanaṃ.example_1: So gantvā satthāraṃ vanditvā satthārā saddhiṃ paṭisammodanaṃ katvā ‘‘ khamanīyaṃ te bhikkhu, kiñci atirekaṃ aphāsukaṃ atthī ’’ ti pucchito āha –
paṭisammodanaṃ.translation_1: Having arrived, he saluted the Teacher, exchanged friendly greetings, and when asked, “Is it bearable, bhikkhu? Do you have any excessive discomfort?” he replied:

paṭigantvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the sentence it means 'having returned' (to the monastery). Some editions read paṭigantvā for patigantvā; the prefix is pati-.
paṭigantvā.example_1: Satthāpi bhikkhusaṅghaṃ ādāya puna māsamatteneva sīvalittherassa puññaṃ anubhavamāno paṭigantvā pubbārāmaṃ pāvisi.
paṭigantvā.translation_1: The Teacher, taking the Sangha of bhikkhus, again enjoyed the merit of the Elder Sīvali for a month, returned, and entered Pubbārāma.

vilimpitunti.meaning_2: to smear; to apply (ointment); to anoint
vilimpitunti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The form is vilimpituṃ + ti (quotative/end-ti). Infinitive in -tuṃ of vilimpati (vi + √lip); root_base and sign are uncertain as the infinitive is built directly on the root.

upajjissatīti.meaning_2: will arise; will be born; will appear
upajjissatīti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Future 3rd singular with the quotative -iti attached; the -ti is part of the quotation, not the verb ending.

avaruddhakopi.meaning_2: opponent; enemy; one to be expelled; name of a demon (Avaruddhaka)
avaruddhakopi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name of a demon in the Dhammapada commentary; the -pi is the emphatic particle 'also'. Nominative singular in the text.
avaruddhakopi.example_1: Avaruddhakopi tatheva paṭikkami, satthāpi sabbarattiṃ parittamakāsi.
avaruddhakopi.translation_1: Avaruddhaka also retreated in the same way, and the Teacher performed the protective recitation throughout the entire night.

ḍaṃsituṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Infinitive used with na icchati, na visahati and na sakkoti in the text.
ḍaṃsituṃ.example_1: Tesaṃ vacanaṃ sutvā ‘‘ iminā attānaṃ ḍaṃsāpetvā marissāmī ’’ ti ‘‘ āharatha, ahaṃ taṃ chaḍḍessāmī ’’ ti tesaṃ hatthato kuṭaṃ gahetvā ekasmiṃ ṭhāne nisinno tena sappena attānaṃ ḍaṃsāpeti, sappo ḍaṃsituṃ na icchati.
ḍaṃsituṃ.translation_1: Hearing their words, he thought, “I will let this snake bite me and die.” He said, “Bring it here; I will throw it away.” He took the jar from their hands, sat down in a certain place, and made the snake bite him. The snake did not wish to bite.
ḍaṃsituṃ.example_2: ‘‘ Bhikkhave, so tāva sappo imassa ito tatiye attabhāve dāso ahosi, so attano sāmikassa sarīraṃ ḍaṃsituṃ na visahatī ’’ ti.
ḍaṃsituṃ.translation_2: “Bhikkhus, that snake was his slave in his third previous existence, and it did not dare to bite the body of its own master.”

vikkiritvā.meaning_2: having scattered; having spread out; having let down (hair)
vikkiritvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in -tvā of vikkirati; here used of letting down the hair (kese vikkiritvā).
vikkiritvā.example_1: Sāpi pātova kiliṭṭhaṃ vatthaṃ nivāsetvā kese vikkiritvā kuṇḍakena sarīraṃ makkhitvā kuṭaṃ ādāya dāsīhi saddhiṃ gacchantī viya gharā nikkhamitvā taṃ ṭhānaṃ agamāsi.
vikkiritvā.translation_1: She, too, early in the morning, robed herself in soiled garments, let her hair down, smeared her body with grain powder, took a waterpot, and as if going with slave-maidens, left the house and went to that place.

sūsūti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] An onomatopoeic indeclinable imitating a hissing sound. In the text it is followed by the quotative particle ti.

paṭitācārattā.meaning_2: because of good conduct; from having mended her ways
paṭitācārattā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Ablative of cause in -ttā from the abstract noun paṭitācāra (good conduct), here explaining the name Paṭācārā; the text's form is built on the Sanskritising paṭita-, while the name itself shows paṭa-. Alternative analysis as ablative of paṭitācāra with the suffix -ttā.
paṭitācārattā.translation_1: She obtained higher ordination and, because she had mended her ways, she became known simply as Paṭācārā.

paṭiadāsi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 3rd singular with the prefix paṭi-; the -i- is the augment. In the text it introduces the mother's reply, 'paṭiadāsi' = 'she returned it'.
paṭiadāsi.example_1: Jīvamānā hi katipayā, matakā eva bahukā ’’ ti vutte ‘‘ tena hi gaṇhatha vo siddhatthake, netaṃ mama puttassa bhesajjan ’’ ti paṭiadāsi.
paṭiadāsi.translation_1: “The living are few, the dead are many.” She said, “Then take your mustard seed back, it is not medicine for my son,” and returned it.

cūḷekasāṭakabrāhmaṇavatthu.meaning_2: story of the brahmin Cūḷekasāṭaka; case of the brahmin Cūḷekasāṭaka
cūḷekasāṭakabrāhmaṇavatthu.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the first story in the Dhammapada commentary. Nominative singular in the text. Cūḷekasāṭaka is the name of the brahmin; vatthu here means 'story, case'.
cūḷekasāṭakabrāhmaṇavatthu.translation_1: 1. The story of the Brahmin Cūḷekasāṭaka.
cūḷekasāṭakabrāhmaṇavatthu.translation_2: The Story of the Brahmin Cūḷekasāṭaka, the first.

cūḷekasāṭakabrāhmaṇaṃ.meaning_2: the brahmin Cūḷekasāṭaka; the brahmin with a single small garment
cūḷekasāṭakabrāhmaṇaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Name of the poor brahmin in the Dhammapada commentary to the verse "Abhittharetha kalyāṇe". Accusative singular in the text.
cūḷekasāṭakabrāhmaṇaṃ.example_1: Abhittharetha kalyāṇeti imaṃ dhammadesanaṃ satthā jetavane viharanto cūḷekasāṭakabrāhmaṇaṃ ārabbha kathesi.
cūḷekasāṭakabrāhmaṇaṃ.translation_1: The Teacher told this Dhamma discourse, “Abhittharetha kalyāṇe,” while dwelling at Jetavana, with reference to the Brahmin Cūḷekasāṭaka.

cūḷekasāṭako.meaning_2: Cūḷekasāṭaka; Little Ekasāṭaka (name of a brahmin)
cūḷekasāṭako.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Name of a brahmin in the Dhammapada commentary, the present-day counterpart of Mahāekasāṭaka. Nominative singular in the text.
cūḷekasāṭako.example_1: Vipassidasabalassa kālasmiñhi mahāekasāṭakabrāhmaṇo nāma ahosi, ayaṃ pana etarahi sāvatthiyaṃ cūḷekasāṭako nāma.
cūḷekasāṭako.translation_1: During the time of the Buddha Vipassī, there was a Brahmin named Mahā Ekasāṭaka; this same person is the Cūḷekasāṭaka of Sāvatthī now.

cūḷekasāṭakassa.meaning_2: Cūḷekasāṭaka; Young Ekasāṭaka; name of a brahmin
cūḷekasāṭakassa.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name of a poor brahmin in the Dhammapada commentary. Genitive singular in the text.
cūḷekasāṭakassa.example_1: ‘‘ aho acchariyaṃ cūḷekasāṭakassa kammaṃ, taṃmuhuttameva sabbacatukkaṃ labhi, idāni katena kalyāṇakammena ajjameva vipāko dinno ’’ ti.
cūḷekasāṭakassa.translation_1: “Oh, amazing is the deed of Cūḷekasāṭaka; he received all the four-fold gifts in that very moment; the result of a good deed done now is given today itself.”

anoramitvā.meaning_2: having refrained (from); having abstained (from); having stopped
anoramitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text anoramitvā = na + oramitvā, an absolutive meaning 'without refraining', i.e. not stopping (at one good deed).
anoramitvā.example_1: Tassattho – sace puriso puññaṃ kareyya,‘‘ ekavāraṃ me puññaṃ kataṃ, alaṃ ettāvatā ’’ ti anoramitvā punappunaṃ karotheva.
anoramitvā.translation_1: The meaning is this: if a person should do a good deed, he should not turn away, thinking, “I have done a good deed once; that is enough,” but should do it again and again.

oramitvā.meaning_2: having abstained (from); having refrained (from); having desisted (from)
oramitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is used with atipariccāgato, i.e., 'having abstained from excessive giving'. The form is ava + ram + tvā with the usual -tvā absolutive ending; the vowel of ava is elided before the root.
oramitvā.example_1: Mahāseṭṭhi tayā pacchimakālaṃ anoloketvāva samaṇassa gotamassa sāsane bahuṃ dhanaṃ vippakiṇṇaṃ, idāni duggato hutvāpi taṃ na muñcasiyeva, evaṃ vattamāno katipāheneva ghāsacchādanamattampi na labhissasi, kiṃ te samaṇena gotamena, atipariccāgato oramitvā kammante payojento kuṭumbaṃ saṇṭhāpehīti.
oramitvā.translation_1: “Mahāseṭṭhi, without considering the future, you have squandered much wealth in the Dispensation of the ascetic Gotama. Now that you are destitute, you still do not stop giving. If you continue like this, within a few days you will not even have food to eat or clothes to wear. What use is the ascetic Gotama to you? Refrain from such excessive giving and attend to your business so you can preserve your family wealth,” she said.

paccatī.meaning_2: ripens; gives results (of karma); is experienced; matures
paccatī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Passive/reflexive of pacati. Commentary glosses as vipākaṃ deti. Text has paccatī with sandhi -ī before ti.
paccatī.example_1: Pāpaṃ na paccatīti diṭṭhadhamme vā samparāye vā vipākaṃ na deti, tāva naṃ evaṃ maññati.
paccatī.translation_1: “The evil has not ripened” means: it does not yet yield its result in the present life or in the next. During that time, he thinks of it this way.
