paccatī.example_2: Yadā ca paccatī pāpaṃ, atha pāpo pāpāni passati.
paccatī.translation_2: but when that evil ripens, then the wicked person sees evil results.

paṭisāmitabboti.meaning_2: stores away; puts in order; arranges; tidies up
paṭisāmitabboti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Potential participle paṭisāmitabba ("should be stored") with -ti quotation marker attached; entry given for the underlying verb. Meaning per PEU.

māvamaññethāti.meaning_2: do not despise; do not disregard
māvamaññethāti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of the prohibitive particle mā with the middle voice present verb avamaññetha (from √man, ava + √man) 'you despise'; the -ti at the end is a quotation marker. Found in Dhammapada commentary prose.

vilumpitukāmā.meaning_2: wishing to plunder; wanting to rob
vilumpitukāmā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is nominative plural masculine, agreeing with corā: 'thieves wishing to plunder me'. The first member is the infinitive vilumpituṃ (from vi + √lup) with the final ṃ dropped before kāma.
vilumpitukāmā.example_1: ‘‘ bhante, corā kira maṃ vilumpitukāmā magge ṭhitā,‘ puna nivattissatī ’ ti sutvā itarasmiṃ magge ṭhitā, ahaṃ etto vā ito vā agantvā thokaṃ idheva bhavissāmi, bhadantā idheva vasitukāmā vasantu, gantukāmā attano ruciṃ karontū ’’ ti.
vilumpitukāmā.translation_1: “Venerable sirs, it is said that thieves wishing to plunder me were waiting on the road, and hearing that I would turn back, they are waiting on the other road; I will not go there or here, but will stay right here for a while; may those venerable ones who wish to stay here stay, and those who wish to go, follow their own pleasure.”

ārakkhaṇatthāya.meaning_2: for the purpose of guarding; for protection
ārakkhaṇatthāya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Dative form of the compound ārakkhaṇattha, used adverbially. In the text it modifies the keeping of the daughter under guard.
ārakkhaṇatthāya.example_1: Rājagahe kira ekā seṭṭhidhītā vayappattā sattabhūmikapāsādassa upari sirigabbhe ārakkhaṇatthāya ekaṃ paricārikaṃ datvā mātāpitūhi vāsiyamānā ekadivasaṃ sāyanhasamaye vātapānena antaravīthiṃ olokentī pañca pāsasatāni pañca sūlasatāni ādāya mige vadhitvā jīvamānaṃ ekaṃ kukkuṭamittaṃ nāma nesādaṃ pañca migasatāni vadhitvā tesaṃ maṃsena mahāsakaṭaṃ pūretvā sakaṭadhure nisīditvā maṃsavikkiṇanatthāya nagaraṃ pavisantaṃ disvā tasmiṃ paṭibaddhacittā paricārikāya hatthe paṇṇākāraṃ datvā ‘‘ gaccha, etassa paṇṇākāraṃ datvā gamanakālaṃ ñatvā ehī ’’ ti pesesi.
ārakkhaṇatthāya.translation_1: It is said that a certain daughter of a householder in Rājagaha, upon reaching maturity, was kept in a private room on the seventh floor of a seven-storied palace, being guarded by a female servant. One evening, looking out of the window into the street, she saw a hunter named Kukkuṭamitta—who lived by killing deer with 500 snares and 500 spears—who had killed 500 deer, filled a large cart with their meat, and was entering the city sitting on the pole of the cart to sell the meat; she became attached to him, gave a present into the hand of the servant, and sent her, saying, 'Go, give this present to that man, learn when he leaves, and come back.'

pariyesāpetvā.meaning_2: having caused to search; having had (someone) look for; having sent in search
pariyesāpetvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative absolutive of pariyesāpeti (causative of pariyesati). In the first sentence the parents had others search; in the second the head fisherman had inquiries made.
pariyesāpetvā.example_1: Tassā mātāpitaro ito cito ca pariyesāpetvā apassantā ‘‘ matā bhavissatī ’’ ti matakabhattaṃ kariṃsu.
pariyesāpetvā.translation_1: Her mother and father looked here and there, and not seeing her, thought, 'She must be dead,' and performed funeral rites.
pariyesāpetvā.example_2: Kevaṭṭajeṭṭhako ‘‘ atthi nu kho imasmiṃ gāme aññepi dārakā ajja jātā ’’ ti pariyesāpetvā tesaṃ jātabhāvaṃ ñatvā ‘‘ ete mama puttassa sahāyakā bhavissantī ’’ ti sabbesaṃ posāvanikaṃ dāpesi.
pariyesāpetvā.translation_2: The head fisherman asked, “Are there any other children born in this village today?” and upon learning of their birth, he provided sustenance for them all, thinking, “These will be the playmates of my son.”

āmānanda.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of the particle āma (yes) with the vocative Ānanda. Occurs at the start of direct speech, addressing Ānanda.
āmānanda.example_1: Āmānanda, so attapañcadasamo acalasaddhāya patiṭṭhāya tīsu ratanesu nikkaṅkho hutvā pāṇātipātakammassa akārako jātoti.
āmānanda.translation_1: “Yes, Ānanda, he, together with the fifteen, became innocent of the act of killing, having been established in unwavering faith and having no doubt in the Three Jewels.”
āmānanda.example_2: ‘‘ Āmānanda, mama santike dhammaṃ sutvā arahattaṃ pattā ’’ ti.
āmānanda.translation_2: “Yes, Ānanda; they attained arahantship after hearing the Dhamma in my presence.”

anuḍahituṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Infinitive expressing the effect of poison on a wound; in the text the simplex verb is gaṇhantassa and anuḍahituṃ is the result clause.
anuḍahituṃ.example_1: Pāṇitalasmiñhi vaṇe asati visaṃ gaṇhantassa taṃ visaṃ anuḍahituṃ na sakkoti, evamevaṃ akusalacetanāya abhāvena pāpaṃ akarontassa dhanuādīni nīharitvā dadatopi pāpaṃ nāma na hotī ’’ ti vatvā anusandhiṃ ghaṭetvā dhammaṃ desento imaṃ gāthamāha –
anuḍahituṃ.translation_1: “Just as when there is no wound in the palm of the hand, one who handles poison cannot be burnt by it, so too, for one who does not perform evil because of the absence of unwholesome intention, there is no evil in giving bows and such things out of service,” and so saying, he joined the connection and, teaching the Dhamma, spoke this verse—

khacitvā.meaning_2: having inlaid; having set with gold; having adorned
khacitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in -itvā of khacati (adorn, inlay). In the sentence it describes decorating bricks with gold.
khacitvā.example_1: Te haritālamanosilā koṭṭetvā tilatelena saṃsanditvā iṭṭhakāya ghaṭetvā suvaṇṇena khacitvā anto ciniṃsu, bahimukhe pana ekagghanasuvaṇṇaiṭṭhakāva ahesuṃ.
khacitvā.translation_1: They reduced the yellow orpiment and red arsenic to a powder, mixed it with sesame oil, and, joining bricks with it, they layered it with gold to build the inner wall; but the outer wall consisted entirely of solid gold bricks.

luñjitvā.meaning_2: having plucked; having torn off; having mauled
luñjitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive of luñcati 'plucks, tears off'; here of dogs tearing at their master's body. The spelling luñjitvā shows the common c/j alternation before -tvā.
luñjitvā.example_1: Sunakhā ‘‘ thero patito ’’ ti saññāya cīvarantaraṃ pavisitvā attano sāmikaṃ luñjitvā khādantā aṭṭhimattāvasesaṃ kariṃsu.
luñjitvā.translation_1: Thinking, 'The elder has fallen,' the dogs entered beneath the robe, mauled their own master, and ate him, leaving only the bones.

niharitvā.meaning_2: having put out; having stuck out; having removed
niharitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in -tvā of niharati (ni + √har). In the sentence it describes the snake's head being put out of the tree hollow: sīsaṃ niharitvā. Not to be confused with nihata.
niharitvā.example_1: Atīte kireko vejjo vejjakammatthāya gāmaṃ vicaritvā kiñci kammaṃ alabhitvā chātajjhatto nikkhamitvā gāmadvāre sambahule kumārake kīḷante disvā ‘‘ ime sappena ḍaṃsāpetvā tikicchitvā āhāraṃ labhissāmī ’’ ti ekasmiṃ rukkhabile sīsaṃ niharitvā nipannaṃ sappaṃ dassetvā,‘‘ ambho, kumārakā eso sāḷikapotako, gaṇhatha nan ’’ ti āha.
niharitvā.translation_1: In the past, it is said, a physician traveled to a village for medical work, found no work, and being tormented by hunger, went out and saw many children playing at the village gate. Thinking, 'I will have these children bitten by a snake, then treat them, and obtain food,' he showed them a snake lying with its head out of a tree-hollow and said, 'Ah, children, that is a young mynah bird; catch it.'

patieti.meaning_2: returns (to); comes back; looks forward to
patieti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Glossed in the text as pacceti ('returns'). Third person singular present.

pavaṭṭitvā.meaning_2: having rolled; having turned; having rolled away
pavaṭṭitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in -tvā of pavaṭṭati. In the text it describes the rock (pāsāṇo) rolling away by itself. The PEU split pa + vaṭṭa + tvā agrees.
pavaṭṭitvā.example_1: Sattame divase pāsāṇo sayameva pavaṭṭitvā apagato.
pavaṭṭitvā.translation_1: On the seventh day, the rock rolled away of its own accord and departed.

vijahituṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Infinitive of vijahati, used with na sakkoti; the dog could not abandon a former wife.
vijahituṃ.example_1: Kiñcāpi hi anamatagge saṃsāre jāyā vā pati vā abhūtapubbā nāma natthi, avidūre pana attabhāve ñātakesu adhimatto sineho hoti, tasmā so sunakho taṃ vijahituṃ na sakkoti.
vijahituṃ.translation_1: In the beginningless samsara, there is truly no one who has not been a wife or a husband to another; however, the affection for relatives in close existences is extreme; therefore, the dog could not abandon her.

paharitabbo.meaning_2: to be struck; to be hit; should be struck
paharitabbo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Potential participle in the negative instruction 'na paharitabbo' (should not be struck). Nominative singular masculine agreeing with 'paro'.
paharitabbo.example_1: Satthā tesaṃ saddaṃ sutvā ‘‘ kiṃ idan ’’ ti pucchitvā ‘‘ idaṃ nāmā ’’ ti ārocite ‘‘ na, bhikkhave, ito paṭṭhāya bhikkhunā nāma evaṃ kattabbaṃ, yo karoti, so imaṃ nāma āpattiṃ āpajjatī ’’ ti pahāradānasikkhāpadaṃ (pāci.449 ādayo) paññāpetvā,‘‘ bhikkhave, bhikkhunā nāma ‘ yathā ahaṃ, tatheva aññepi daṇḍassa tasanti, maccuno bhāyantī ’ ti ñatvā paro na paharitabbo, na ghātetabbo ’’ ti vatvā anusandhiṃ ghaṭetvā dhammaṃ desento imaṃ gāthamāha –
paharitabbo.translation_1: The Teacher, hearing their noise, asked, “What is this?” When he was told what had happened, he said, “Monks, from now on, a bhikkhu must not do such a thing; whoever does so commits this specific offense.” Having laid down the training rule on giving blows (pahāradānasikkhāpadaṃ) (Pācittiya 74, etc.), he said, “Monks, a bhikkhu, knowing that ‘just as I do, so too others tremble at punishment and fear death,’ should not strike or kill another.” Then, having joined the connection, while teaching the Dhamma, he spoke this verse:
paharitabbo.example_2: Idhāpi satthā tesaṃ saddaṃ sutvā ‘‘ kiṃ idan ’’ ti pucchitvā ‘‘ idaṃ nāmā ’’ ti ārocite ‘‘ na, bhikkhave, ito paṭṭhāya bhikkhunā nāma evaṃ kattabbaṃ, yo karoti, so imaṃ nāma āpattiṃ āpajjatī ’’ ti talasattikasikkhāpadaṃ (pāci.454 ādayo) paññāpetvā,‘‘ bhikkhave, bhikkhunā nāma ‘ yathā ahaṃ, tatheva aññepi daṇḍassa tasanti, yathā ca mayhaṃ, tatheva nesaṃ jīvitaṃ piyan ’ ti ñatvā paro na paharitabbo na ghāṭetabbo ’’ ti vatvā anusandhiṃ ghaṭetvā dhammaṃ desento imaṃ gāthamāha –
paharitabbo.translation_2: In this instance too, the Teacher heard their outcry and asked, “What is that?” When told, “It is this matter,” he said, “Monks, henceforth a bhikkhu should not do such a thing. Whoever does so is guilty of such an offense.” Having thus promulgated the training rule regarding threatening gestures, he said, “Monks, a bhikkhu should consider: ‘Just as I tremble at the rod, so too do others; and just as life is dear to me, so too is it dear to them.’ Knowing this, one should not strike another nor lead another to strike.” Having said this, he linked the connection and, teaching the Dhamma, declared this verse:

ghāṭetabboti.meaning_2: to be killed; to be struck down; to be slain; to be hit
ghāṭetabboti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text the quotation particle ti is attached; the entry is for the main word. Potential participle of the causative ghāṭeti (√ghaṭṭ 1 with -e-). The PEU suggests a possible splitting 'ghaṭa + ṇe + tabba', but the usual analysis is from √ghaṭṭ.

apīcimhi.meaning_2: but here; and here; moreover, in this
apīcimhi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of api + idha (with loss of initial i and change to ī). The text has avīci (Avīci hell) nearby; apīcimhi is not avīci + imhi. Locative sense 'in this (dispensation)'.
apīcimhi.example_1: Devatā apīcimhi nibbattitvā ekaṃ buddhantaraṃ tattha paccitvā imasmiṃ buddhuppāde sāvatthiyaṃ nibbattitvā vuddhimanvāya sāsane pabbajitvā upasampadaṃ labhi.
apīcimhi.translation_1: The devatā was reborn in the Avīci hell, and after suffering there for one Buddha-interval, was reborn in Sāvatthī in this Buddha’s dispensation, and upon growing up, went forth and attained higher ordination.

nidahituṃ.meaning_2: to deposit; to lay aside; to store
nidahituṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Infinitive of nidahati (ni + √dhā). In the text it depends on laddhaṃ, expressing permission to deposit wealth.
nidahituṃ.example_1: ‘‘ ettakaṃ me, tātā, aggiādīhi asādhāraṇe buddhassa sāsane dhanaṃ nidahituṃ laddhaṃ,‘ punapi ettakaṃ dhanaṃ vissajjetvā satthu gandhakuṭiṃ kātuṃ labhissāmī ’ ti tuṭṭhamānaso apphoṭesin ’’ ti.
nidahituṃ.translation_1: “My friends, I have been permitted to deposit so much wealth in the Buddha’s Dispensation, which is not shared by mishaps like fire. Happy-hearted, I clapped, thinking, ‘I shall be permitted to spend an equal amount again to build a Perfumed Chamber for the Teacher.’”

aggiḍaḍḍhova.meaning_2: as if burned by fire; like one scorched by fire
aggiḍaḍḍhova.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of aggiḍaḍḍha (burnt by fire) and iva (like, as if), with elision of the initial i. Used in the simile aggiḍaḍḍhova tappati.
aggiḍaḍḍhova.example_1: Sehi kammehi dummedho, aggiḍaḍḍhova tappatī ’’ ti.
aggiḍaḍḍhova.translation_1: Lacking discerning wisdom, he is tormented by his own actions, as if burned by fire.
aggiḍaḍḍhova.example_2: Sehīti so tehi attano santakehi kammehi dummedho nippañño puggalo niraye nibbattitvā aggiḍaḍḍhova tappatīti attho.
aggiḍaḍḍhova.translation_2: Regarding the word “by his own,” the meaning is that a fool lacking discerning wisdom, having been reborn in hell because of his own actions, is tormented as if burned by fire.

saṃcuṇṇito.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Past participle used as an adjective in the text, agreeing with the subject (nominative singular).
saṃcuṇṇito.example_1: Satthā idaṃ tassa pubbakammaṃ kathetvā,‘‘ bhikkhave, moggallāno ettakaṃ kammaṃ katvā anekavassasatasahassāni niraye paccitvā vipākāvasesena attabhāvasate evameva koṭṭetvā saṃcuṇṇito maraṇaṃ patto.
saṃcuṇṇito.translation_1: The Teacher, having related this past kamma of his, said, “Bhikkhus, Moggallāna, having committed this kamma, suffered in hell for hundreds of thousands of years, and due to the remainder of the result, for a hundred lifetimes he was beaten and crushed to death in the same way.”

kāṇakuṇādibhāvanti.meaning_2: state of being blind, lame and so on; becoming blind or deformed
kāṇakuṇādibhāvanti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound ending in bhāva with -aṃ for -o at the end of the quoted clause (perhaps taken as the object of āpajjati). The text has kāṇakuṇādibhāvanti = kāṇakuṇādibhāvaṃ + iti.
kāṇakuṇādibhāvanti.example_1: Yaṃ hissa gehe dhaññaṃ, taṃ pūtibhāvaṃ āpajjati, suvaṇṇaṃ aṅgārabhāvaṃ, muttā kappāsaṭṭhibhāvaṃ, kahāpaṇaṃ kapālakhaṇḍādibhāvaṃ, dvipadacatuppadā kāṇakuṇādibhāvanti attho.
kāṇakuṇādibhāvanti.translation_1: The meaning is that the grain in his house decays, gold becomes charcoal, pearls become like cotton seeds, coins become like shards of pottery, and his two-footed and four-footed creatures become blind or deformed.

upatthambhayamāno.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Present participle masculine nominative singular, agreeing with satthā. The Teacher is supporting (reassuring) the monk before rebuking him. Some editions read upatthambhayamāno for upatthambhayanto; the -aya- is the causative sign.
upatthambhayamāno.example_1: Atha naṃ satthā upatthambhayamāno nanu tvaṃ bhikkhu pubbe hirottappagavesako dakarakkhasakālepi hirottappaṃ gavesamāno dvādasa vassāni vihāsi, kasmā idāni evaṃ garuke buddhasāsane pabbajitvā catuparisamajjhe pārupanaṃ chaḍḍetvā hirottappaṃ pahāya ṭhitosīti.
upatthambhayamāno.translation_1: Then the Teacher, supporting him, said, “Bhikkhu, in the past you sought moral shame and dread; even when you were a water-demon, you sought moral shame and dread for twelve years, did you not? Yet now, having gone forth in such a respectful dispensation of the Buddha, why do you stand here in the midst of the fourfold assembly having discarded your outer robe and abandoned moral shame and dread?”

bhisamulālaṃ.meaning_2: lotus stalks and (edible) lotus roots; lotus stems and tubers
bhisamulālaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text, object of khāditvā. A dvanda compound of bhisa (lotus stalk) and mulāla (lotus root, edible tuber); the two parts are often written as one word and mean edible aquatic plants. bhisamulālaṃ}
bhisamulālaṃ.example_1: ‘‘ bho purisa, tvaṃ maggakilanto, kasmā imaṃ saraṃ otaritvā nhatvā ca pivitvā ca bhisamulālaṃ khāditvā pupphāni pilandhitvā na gacchasī ’’ ti.
bhisamulālaṃ.translation_1: “Friend, you are tired from the journey; why do you not descend into this lake, bathe and drink, eat the lotus stalks and bulbs, adorn yourself with flowers, and then be on your way?”

sitapātukaraṇe.meaning_2: display of a smile; showing a smile; manifestation of smiling
sitapātukaraṇe.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound of sita (smile) + pātukaraṇa (manifestation). Locative singular in the text; the commentary also uses the variant sitapātukamma.
sitapātukaraṇe.example_1: Satthā sitaṃ katvā ‘‘ ko nu kho, bhante, sitapātukaraṇe hetū ’’ ti ānandattherena puṭṭho sitakāraṇaṃ ācikkhanto āha –
sitapātukaraṇe.translation_1: The Teacher smiled. When asked by the Elder Ānanda, “Venerable sir, what is the reason for this display of a smile?” he explained the reason and said—

aṭṭhasuṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 3rd plural aorist. Doubtful: possibly aṭṭhaṃsu with assimilation; the root √ṭhā is suggested by the sense 'stood'.
aṭṭhasuṃ.example_1: Nāṭakā parivāretvā aṭṭhasuṃ, tassa purato bhattapātiṃ vaḍḍhetvā ṭhapayiṃsu.
aṭṭhasuṃ.translation_1: At the time of washing his hands, a certain Paccekabuddha on Mount Gandhamādana arose from absorption after seven days and, thinking, “Where shall I go today for alms?”, saw Bhattabhatika.

asanisatanipākasaddo.meaning_2: the sound of a hundred thunderbolts striking; the noise of a hundred simultaneous peals of thunder
asanisatanipākasaddo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of asanisata (a hundred thunderbolts) and nipākasaddo (the sound of striking); nominative singular, used in a simile for a great roar of applause. Alternatively asanisatani + pākasaddo.
asanisatanipākasaddo.example_1: Mahājano paccekabuddhānaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ vibhajitvā diyyamānaṃ disvā sādhukārasahassāni pavattesi, asanisatanipākasaddo viya ahosi.
asanisatanipākasaddo.translation_1: Seeing the almsfood being divided and given to the private Buddhas, the populace raised thousands of shouts of applause; it was like the sound of a hundred simultaneous peals of thunder.

guṇātirekasampadāti.meaning_2: accomplishment of surpassing virtue; perfection of excellent qualities
guṇātirekasampadāti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] One of four sampadā listed in the Dhammapada commentary. Ends in -ti in the text as part of the quotation; the headword is the compound itself.
guṇātirekasampadāti.example_1: Catasso hi sampadā nāma – vatthusampadā, paccayasampadā, cetanāsampadā, guṇātirekasampadāti.
guṇātirekasampadāti.translation_1: There are indeed four accomplishments: accomplishment of substance, accomplishment of requisites, accomplishment of intention, and accomplishment of great virtue.

madavegena.meaning_2: force of intoxication; impetus of pride; momentum of drunkenness
madavegena.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Instrumental singular in the text ("with the force of intoxication"). Compound of mada (intoxication, pride) and vega (force, impetus).
madavegena.example_1: Tāpi madavegena kampamānasarīrā ‘‘ iccāma, gāyāmā ’’ ti cittaṃ uppādesuṃ.
madavegena.translation_1: They, their bodies swaying with the force of intoxication, conceived the desire to dance and sing.

iccāma.meaning_2: thus we wish; so let us; we want to
iccāma.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of iti and the 1st person plural present of √i (ema/āma), used in the phrase 'iccāma, gāyāmā' expressing a wish; some editions treat iccāma as a variant of icchāma (from √is).
iccāma.example_1: Tāpi madavegena kampamānasarīrā ‘‘ iccāma, gāyāmā ’’ ti cittaṃ uppādesuṃ.
iccāma.translation_1: They, their bodies swaying with the force of intoxication, conceived the desire to dance and sing.

kahāpaṇāni.meaning_2: kahāpaṇa; a unit of money; silver coin
kahāpaṇāni.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative plural in the text, the amount of the fine. The related PEU entries kahāpaṇaka and kahāpaṇika are adjectives derived from kahāpaṇa, not this noun.
kahāpaṇāni.example_1: ‘‘ ṭhapetvā geharakkhake dārake sirimāya dassanatthaṃ anāgacchantānaṃ aṭṭha kahāpaṇāni daṇḍo ’’ ti.
kahāpaṇāni.translation_1: “Except for house-guards, those who do not come to see Sirimā shall be fined eight kahāpaṇas.”

anibbattantiyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Present participle feminine instrumental/locative/ablative singular. Used metaphorically of rebirth in the Tusita heaven; the text may be read as 'since she was not reborn there'.
anibbattantiyā.example_1: Tusitabhavane, mahārājāti, bhante, tāya tusitabhavane anibbattantiyā ko añño nibbattissati, bhante, natthi tāya sadisā itthī.
anibbattantiyā.translation_1: “In the Tusita realm, Great King.” “Venerable Sir, if she was not reborn in the Tusita realm, who else could be reborn there? Venerable Sir, there is no woman like her.”

katapaṭisammodano.meaning_2: greeted in return; having exchanged greetings (with)
katapaṭisammodano.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it describes the king as tuṭṭhacittena katapaṭisammodano, i.e. he was greeted in return by the Brahmin. Some manuscripts read 'katapaṭisammodano' with a sandhi consonant. The PEU's 'one who has been preaching' is doubtful.
katapaṭisammodano.example_1: So hi saṃvaccharamattena taṃ gāthaṃ paguṇaṃ katvā paguṇabhāvaṃ puttassa ārocetvā ‘‘ tena hi, tāta, kañcideva paṇṇākāraṃ ādāya āgacchatha, ahaṃ purimataraṃ gantvā rañño santike ṭhassāmī ’’ ti vutte ‘‘ sādhu, tātā ’’ ti paṇṇākāraṃ gahetvā somadattassa rañño santike ṭhitakāle ussāhappatto rājakulaṃ gantvā raññā tuṭṭhacittena katapaṭisammodano,‘‘ tāta, cirassaṃ vata āgatattha, idamāsanaṃ nisīditvā vadatha, yenattho ’’ ti vutte imaṃ gāthamāha –
katapaṭisammodano.translation_1: The brahmin spent a year learning the verse by heart. When he had perfected it, he told his son. “Very well, father, bring some gift and follow me. I will go ahead and wait in the king’s presence.” He replied, “Very well, dear son,” and took a gift. As Somadatta waited in the king’s presence, the brahmin, exerting himself, went to the royal palace. The king, delighted, greeted him cordially: “Father, you have come a long way. Sit here and tell me what you need.” When he said this, the brahmin pronounced this verse—

jute.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative singular in the text (jute = jute, 'clever at dicing'). Probably from √jut 'shine' in the sense of bright, clever. Sometimes taken as a by-form of jūta (gambling), but the meaning here is 'skilled'.
jute.example_1: So satenapi satadvayenapi suraṃ āharāpetvā pivanto iminā anukkameneva nisinnaṭṭhānādīsu kahāpaṇarāsiṃ ṭhapetvā suraṃ pivanto ‘‘ iminā mālā āharatha, iminā gandhe, ayaṃ jano jute cheko, ayaṃ nacce, ayaṃ gīte, ayaṃ vādite.
jute.translation_1: He spent 100 or 200 on liquor, and while drinking, he would place a heap of coins and say, “Take this coin to fetch flowers, take this for perfumes; this man is clever at dicing, this at dancing, this at singing, and this at playing music.

uppāṭetuṃ.meaning_2: to pluck out; to pull out; to root out
uppāṭetuṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Infinitive of uppāṭeti (causative of uppaṭati), meaning 'to pluck out, tear out' (eyes). In the text it depends on vaṭṭati ('it is fitting ... to pluck out').
uppāṭetuṃ.example_1: Imaṃ mayā māretuṃ vā hatthapāde vāssa chindituṃ akkhīni vā uppāṭetuṃ vaṭṭati, evaṃ aññassa pāsādaṃ na karissatī ’’ ti.
uppāṭetuṃ.translation_1: It would be fitting for me to kill him, cut off his hands and feet, or pluck out his eyes; for if I do this, he will build such a palace for no one else.”

pavesatvā.meaning_2: having caused to enter; having brought in; having sent in
pavesatvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative absolutive of pavesati (pa + √vis, causative). The related PEU entry pavesati has visa (not vis) in the split; here the root is taken as √vis 1 with the causative sign *e. In the text it takes antonivesanaṃ as its object.
pavesatvā.example_1: So dussāni saṃharitvā satthāraṃ antonivesanaṃ pavesatvā yāgukhajjakena sammānetvā ekamantaṃ nisinno vanditvā āha –
pavesatvā.translation_1: The prince rolled up the cloths, escorted the Teacher inside, honored him with rice-porridge and hard food, and sat to one side and said—

gīhī.meaning_2: householder; layman; one who lives at home
gīhī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Nominative singular used as subject; the form is identical to the stem (gīhī) and appears in the phrase gīhī samāno. Often contrasted with pabbajita.
gīhī.example_1: Tattha sace gīhī samāno ‘‘ attānaṃ rakkhissāmī ’’ ti uparipāsādatale susaṃvutaṃ gabbhaṃ pavisitvā sampannārakkho hutvā vasantopi, pabbajito hutvā susaṃvute pihitadvāravātapāne leṇe viharantopi attānaṃ na rakkhatiyeva.
gīhī.translation_1: Among those who guard themselves, if a householder thinks, “I will guard myself,” and enters a room with closed doors on the upper floor of a palace and lives there perfectly secure, or if a renunciant lives in a cave with closed doors and windows, he is not truly guarding himself.

anivesetvā.meaning_2: not having established; not having settled; not having placed
anivesetvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Negative absolutive of niveseti, in the phrase attānaṃ anivesetvā (not having established oneself).
anivesetvā.example_1: Attānañhi tattha anivesetvā kevalaṃ parameva anusāsamāno parato nindaṃ labhitvā kilissati nāma, tattha attānaṃ nivesetvā anusāsamāno parato pasaṃsaṃ labhati, tasmā na kilissati nāma.
anivesetvā.translation_1: For, if one instructs only others without first establishing oneself therein, one is stained, having received blame from others; but if one instructs others after having established oneself therein, one receives praise from others; therefore, one is not stained.

disoti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Doubled form of the verb passive disati. The lemma_2 guide disodhi is unrelated; disoti is disati in a different guise.

ottharantī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Feminine present participle ottharantī, nominative singular agreeing with māluvā; here the creeper is said to cover (ottharantī) the sāla tree.
ottharantī.example_1: Māluvā sālamivotthatanti yassa puggalassa taṃ taṇhāsaṅkhātaṃ dussīlyaṃ yathā nāma māluvā sālaṃ ottharantī deve vassante pattehi udakaṃ sampaṭicchitvā sambhañjanavasena sabbatthakameva pariyonandhati, evaṃ attabhāvaṃ otthataṃ pariyonandhitvā ṭhitaṃ.
ottharantī.translation_1: ‘Like a creeper over a sāla tree’ means that for the person whose depravity—which is craving—is like a creeper that, while covering a sāla tree, receives water in its leaves when it rains, and by the power of its crushing, covers the entire tree—it covers and remains wrapped around his existence.

pātiyamāno.meaning_2: causing to fall; making fall down; dropping
pātiyamāno.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Present participle masculine nominative singular, passive/causative sense. In the text it describes a tree being made to fall. PED's pata + ṇaya analysis supports the causative meaning.
pātiyamāno.example_1: So māluvāya sambhañjitvā bhūmiyaṃ pātiyamāno rukkho viya tāya dussīlyasaṅkhātāya taṇhāya sambhañjitvā apāyesu pātiyamāno, yathā naṃ anatthakāmo diso icchati, tathā attānaṃ karoti nāmāti attho.
pātiyamāno.translation_1: Just as a tree that is crushed by a creeper and falls to the ground, he is crushed by that craving known as depravity and is cast into the states of deprivation; it means he brings upon himself exactly what his enemy, wishing for his ruin, desires.

paṇaye.meaning_2: applies; carries out; establishes; brings about
paṇaye.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Optative 3rd singular in -e (paṇaye) after ''Issaro ... daṇḍaṃ'', 'one would apply punishment'. Could also be optative of paṇayati in the sense 'should be carried out'.
paṇaye.example_1: Issaro paṇaye daṇḍaṃ, sāmaṃ appaṭivekkhiyā ’’ ti.
paṇaye.translation_1: And who applies punishment without reflecting upon himself,”

khipāpetvā.meaning_2: having caused to throw; having had (her) thrown
khipāpetvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative absolutive of khipati (to throw); the causative khipāpeti means 'causes to throw, has thrown'. In the text the king has the woman thrown into the robbers' pit.
khipāpetvā.example_1: Rājā taṃ uddhaṃpādaṃ gahetvā corapapāte khipāpetvā nagaraṃ pavisitvā dhammena rajjaṃ kāresi.
khipāpetvā.translation_1: The king caught her, had her thrown upside down into the robbers’ precipice, entered the city, and ruled by Dhamma.

nimiletvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in -tvā of the causative nimīleti, used of the eyes (akkhīni nimiletvā).
nimiletvā.example_1: Hatthipotako vāladhiṃ antarasatthimhi pakkhipitvā ubho kaṇṇe pātetvā akkhīni nimiletvā aṭṭhāsi.
nimiletvā.translation_1: The baby elephant tucked his tail between his legs, let down both ears, closed his eyes, and stood.

noyāti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of na uyyāti (= na + uyyāti, 'does not go away; cannot follow'); some editions have noyāti / noyāti.
noyāti.translation_1: Whose victory no one in the world can follow;

noyātīti.meaning_2: does not go; does not come to; is not included
noyātīti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of na + yāti with the quotation particle -ti; here treated as the resolved reading no + yāti + iti (na + yāti + iti), i.e. 'it does not go'. If analysed as sandhi of no (na + o) + yāti, the entry could instead be noyāti, pos sandhi.

saṃbhajjamāno.meaning_2: being broken; being shattered; being split apart
saṃbhajjamāno.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Present participle masculine nominative singular, agreeing with rattacandanarukkho. The prefix saṃ- here means 'apart, to pieces'; the passive sense 'being shattered' fits the context of the tree broken on the rocks. Some editions may read sambhajjamāno.
saṃbhajjamāno.example_1: Atheko rattacandanarukkho gaṅgāya uparitīre jāto gaṅgodakena dhotamūlo patitvā tattha tattha pāsāṇesu saṃbhajjamāno vippakiri.
saṃbhajjamāno.translation_1: Now, a red sandalwood tree that had grown on the bank upstream of the Ganges had its roots washed away, fell, and was shattered into pieces by the rocks here and there.

pothiyamānā.meaning_2: being ground; being crushed; being pounded
pothiyamānā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Feminine nominative singular agreeing with ghaṭikā. Describes the clay fragment being worn down by waves; passive sense of the present participle.
pothiyamānā.example_1: Tato ekā ghaṭappamāṇā ghaṭikā pāsāṇehi ghaṃsiyamānā udakaūmīhi pothiyamānā maṭṭhā hutvā anupubbena vuyhamānā sevālapariyonaddhā āgantvā tassa jāle laggi.
pothiyamānā.translation_1: From there, a fragment the size of a water jar, polished by rubbing against rocks and pounded by the waves, drifted along and, becoming wrapped in Blyxa plants, eventually came and got caught in the rich man's basket.

olambāpetvā.meaning_2: having caused to hang; having caused to dangle
olambāpetvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative absolutive of olambāpeti; the object (pattaṃ) is hung from a cord and bamboo contraption. Sometimes written with ava- as o-.
olambāpetvā.example_1: Gehe bhamaṃ yojetvā pattaṃ likhāpetvā sikkāya ṭhapetvā veḷuparamparāya saṭṭhihatthamatte ākāse olambāpetvā ‘ sace arahā atthi, imaṃ ākāsenāgantvā gaṇhātū ’ ti vakkhāmi.
olambāpetvā.translation_1: I will have a lathe set up in my house, have a bowl turned, suspend it from a cord, and with a series of bamboos, hang it sixty cubits high in the air, and I will declare: ‘If an arahant exists, let him come through the air and take this bowl.’

kaṇḍambarukkhotveva.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of kaṇḍambarukkho + iva (= eva in the text). kaṇḍamba appears to be a tree name; rukkho is 'tree'. Unattested elsewhere; no sentence supplied, so the case cannot be confirmed.

uppāṭāpitā.meaning_2: caused to be pulled up; had (a sapling) uprooted
uppāṭāpitā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Past participle used passively; nominative plural agreeing with ambapotakā in the text.
uppāṭāpitā.example_1: Dhuttakāpi ambapakkāni khāditvā ‘‘ hare duṭṭhatitthiyā ‘ samaṇo kira gotamo kaṇḍambarukkhamūle pāṭihāriyaṃ karissatī ’ ti tumhehi yojanabbhantare tadahujātāpi ambapotakā uppāṭāpitā, kaṇḍambo nāma ayan ’’ ti vatvā te ucchiṭṭhaambaṭṭhīhi pahariṃsu.
uppāṭāpitā.translation_1: The rogues also ate the ripe mangoes (amb p akkani) and said, “Hey, you wicked sectarians! You had even the mango saplings that sprouted today pulled up (uppāṭāpitā) within a league's distance because you heard that the ascetic Gotama would perform a miracle at the root of the Kaṇḍamba mango tree. Well, this is the Kaṇḍamba mango tree!” and they struck them with the discarded mango stones.

kaṇḍambo.meaning_2: Kaṇḍamba mango tree; name of a mango tree
kaṇḍambo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Nominative singular in the text; the tree under which the Buddha performed the miracle.
kaṇḍambo.example_1: Dhuttakāpi ambapakkāni khāditvā ‘‘ hare duṭṭhatitthiyā ‘ samaṇo kira gotamo kaṇḍambarukkhamūle pāṭihāriyaṃ karissatī ’ ti tumhehi yojanabbhantare tadahujātāpi ambapotakā uppāṭāpitā, kaṇḍambo nāma ayan ’’ ti vatvā te ucchiṭṭhaambaṭṭhīhi pahariṃsu.
kaṇḍambo.translation_1: The rogues also ate the ripe mangoes (amb p akkani) and said, “Hey, you wicked sectarians! You had even the mango saplings that sprouted today pulled up (uppāṭāpitā) within a league's distance because you heard that the ascetic Gotama would perform a miracle at the root of the Kaṇḍamba mango tree. Well, this is the Kaṇḍamba mango tree!” and they struck them with the discarded mango stones.

cīreti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative form of √car used intransitively in the sense of living or behaving. No sentences were supplied, so the meaning is inferred from the root and from the related cīra entries.

bālāpuṭo.meaning_2: fool's bundle; bundle of fools; seal of stupidity
bālāpuṭo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Nominal compound of bāla (fool) + puṭa (bundle, container). Nominative singular in the text, describing something bound or sealed by foolishness; possibly a nickname or textual variant.
bālāpuṭo.example_1: Atha naṃ satthā ‘‘ nāyaṃ moggallānaṃ tavatthāya baddho bālāpuṭo.
bālāpuṭo.translation_1: Then the Teacher said to him, “Moggallāna, this task was not intended for you.

udaddhari.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 3rd singular of uddharati; object is garuṃ bhāraṃ.
udaddhari.translation_1: The one who spoke pleasantly pulled a very heavy burden;

idhaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant of idha with emphatic particle iṃ; some take it as imaṃ (this). In the text it opens the sentence: 'Here the Tathāgata performs...'.
idhaṃ.example_1: Idhaṃ tathāgato yamakapāṭihāriyaṃ karoti asādhāraṇaṃ sāvakehi, uparimakāyato aggikkhandho pavattati, heṭṭhimakāyato udakadhārā pavattati.
idhaṃ.translation_1: Here, the Tathāgata performs the Twin Miracle, not shared by his disciples. A flame of fire proceeds from the upper part of his body, and a stream of water from the lower part.

nimaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of na + imaṃ, meaning 'not this' = 'not this world'. Alternative analysis: na + imaṃ with nimaṃ as the sandhi form. Accusative singular of ima in the text.
nimaṃ.translation_1: “The wise one, delighting in solitude, will not come back to this world.

ekarukkhadoṇikanāvappamāṇo.meaning_2: the size of a single-log boat; as large as a dugout canoe made from one tree
ekarukkhadoṇikanāvappamāṇo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound with a assimilated nāvā > nāva (sandhi before pamāṇa); used in the Dhammapada commentary of the Nāga king Erakapatta's size.
ekarukkhadoṇikanāvappamāṇo.example_1: So ‘‘ appamattakaṃ etan ’’ ti āpattiṃ adesetvā vīsati vassasahassāni araññe samaṇadhammaṃ katvāpi maraṇakāle erakapattena gīvāya gahito viya āpattiṃ desetukāmopi aññaṃ bhikkhuṃ apassamāno ‘‘ aparisuddhaṃ me sīlan ’’ ti uppannavippaṭisāro tato cavitvā ekarukkhadoṇikanāvappamāṇo nāgarājā hutvā nibbatti, erakapatto tvevassa nāmaṃ ahosi.
ekarukkhadoṇikanāvappamāṇo.translation_1: Thinking, “This is only a trifle,” he did not confess the offense. Although he performed ascetic practices in the forest for twenty thousand years, at the time of death, it felt as though an Erakapatta leaf were pulling at his throat. Wishing to confess but seeing no other bhikkhu, he was filled with remorse, thinking, “My virtue is not pure.” Upon death, he was reborn as a Nāga king the size of a dugout boat. He was named “Erakapatta.”

naccāpetvā.meaning_2: having made dance; having caused to dance
naccāpetvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative absolutive of naccati; the object is the daughter, so 'having made (her) dance'. Part of a causative verb pair with gāyāpesi.
naccāpetvā.example_1: So aparabhāge ekaṃ dhītaraṃ labhitvā majjhe gaṅgāya udakapiṭṭhe mahantaṃ phalaṃ ukkhipitvā dhītaraṃ tasmiṃ ṭhapetvā naccāpetvā gāyāpesi.
naccāpetvā.translation_1: Later, he had a daughter. Spreading his great hood on the surface of the Ganges, he placed his daughter upon it and had her dance and sing.

vodāpanaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Commentary gloss on sacittapariyodapanaṃ; nominative singular in the text.
vodāpanaṃ.translation_1: “Purifying one’s own heart” is the purifying of one’s own mind from the five hindrances.

anūpavādāpanañca.meaning_2: and causing (others) not to insult; and not inciting to insult
anūpavādāpanañca.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of anūpavādāpanaṃ (neuter nominative/accusative of anūpavādāpana, 'causing to insult' or, with na, 'causing not to insult') + ca; glossed in the text as anūpavādanaṃ and anūpavādāpanaṃ, contrasting with anūpavāda.
anūpavādāpanañca.translation_1: “Not insulting” means neither insulting oneself nor causing others to insult.

upakappanakakāmehi.meaning_2: beneficial; useful; bringing benefit; ready for use
upakappanakakāmehi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Instrumental plural agreeing with kāmehi; adjective formed from upakappana ('benefit, service') with suffix -ka.
upakappanakakāmehi.example_1: Api dibbesūti sace hi devānaṃ upakappanakakāmehi nimanteyyāpi āyasmā samiddhi viya evampi tesu kāmesu ratiṃ na vindatiyeva.
upakappanakakāmehi.translation_1: “Even in heavenly” means: if one were invited with sensual pleasures created by the power of merit of the devas, even then, like the Elder Samiddhi who was invited by a deva, one does not find delight in those sensual pleasures.

dhūmāyituṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Infinitive dhūmāyituṃ in the text; the verb is formed from dhūma with the affix āya, as is the absolutive dhūmāyitvā.
dhūmāyituṃ.example_1: Thero ‘‘ ayaṃ nāgarājā ‘ ahameva dhūmāyituṃ sakkomi, aññe na sakkontī ’ ti maññe sallakkhetī ’’ ti sayampi dhūmāyi.
dhūmāyituṃ.translation_1: The Elder thought, “This Nāga king thinks, ‘I alone can blow smoke; others cannot,’ ” so he blew smoke himself.

goājanīyo.meaning_2: thoroughbred bull; excellent ox; noble bull
goājanīyo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] One of the four ājanīya (thoroughbreds) in the sutta simile: hatthājānīya, assājanīya, goājanīya, purisājānīya. Nominative singular in the text.
goājanīyo.example_1: ‘‘ hatthājānīyo chaddantakule vā uposathakule vā uppajjati, assājānīyo sindhavakule vā valāhakassarājakule vā, usabho goājanīyo dakkhiṇapathetiādīni vadantena satthārā hatthiājānīyādīnaṃ uppattiṭṭhānādīni kathitāni, purisājānīyo pana kahaṃ nu kho uppajjatī ’’ ti.
goājanīyo.translation_1: 'The Teacher, while speaking of such things as, "An excellent thoroughbred elephant is born in the Chaddanta or Uposatha lineage; an excellent thoroughbred horse in the Sindh or Valāhaka horse-king lineage; an excellent thoroughbred bullock in the Deccan," has explained the birthplaces of noble thoroughbreds. But where does the noble thoroughbred person arise?'

anabhivanditvā.meaning_2: not having venerated; without venerating; without paying respects (to)
anabhivanditvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Negative absolutive (na + abhivanditvā) in the text, modifying brāhmaṇo; object tathāgataṃ is in accusative.
anabhivanditvā.example_1: So brāhmaṇo āgantvā tathāgataṃ anabhivanditvā tameva devaṭṭhānaṃ vanditvā aṭṭhāsi.
anabhivanditvā.translation_1: That brahmin came, but without venerating the Tathāgata, he venerated only the sacred site and stood there.

ñāātikalahavūpasamanavatthu.meaning_2: case of the settling of a quarrel among relatives
ñāātikalahavūpasamanavatthu.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of a Dhammapada commentary story. The first element ñāāti is a spelling with double ā; normally ñāti. Compound with vatthu meaning 'case' as in Vinaya texts.
ñāātikalahavūpasamanavatthu.translation_1: 1. The Story of the Settlement of the Quarrel Among Relatives

abhibhūyamānopi.meaning_2: being overcome (by); being overpowered (by); being overwhelmed (by)
abhibhūyamānopi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Present participle passive of abhibhavati with the particle -pi; here in the phrase niddāya abhibhūyamānopi, 'though being overcome by sleep'.
abhibhūyamānopi.example_1: Ekadivasaṃ bhuttapātarāso bhattasammadaṃ avinodetvā satthu santikaṃ gantvā kilantarūpo ito cito ca samparivattati, niddāya abhibhūyamānopi ujukaṃ nipajjituṃ asakkonto ekamantaṃ nisīdi.
abhibhūyamānopi.translation_1: One day, having finished breakfast and not having dispelled the drowsiness caused by the meal, he went to the Teacher’s presence, looking weary, rolling around from one side to the other, and though overcome by sleep, not being able to lie down straight, he sat to one side.

vajīrakumāriṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Name of a daughter given in marriage; accusative singular in the text.
vajīrakumāriṃ.example_1: Pubbe me bhāgineyyena saddhiṃ yuddhameva hoti, idāni vajīrakumāriṃ nāma dhītaraṃ bhāgineyyassa datvā so gāmo tassāyeva nhānacuṇṇamūlaṃ katvā dinno, tena saddhiṃ viggaho vūpasanto, imināpi me kāraṇena sukhameva jātaṃ.
vajīrakumāriṃ.translation_1: “Formerly, I had nothing but strife with my nephew; but now I have given my daughter, Vajirā, to my nephew, and that village was given to her to cover the cost of her bathing powder; the strife with him has subsided, and for this reason also I am happy.”

upaṭṭhahituṃ.meaning_2: to attend (to); to look after; to nurse; to serve
upaṭṭhahituṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Infinitive in -tuṃ of upaṭṭhahati; here with gilāne, 'to attend to the sick'. The vowel -a- before -hi- is a present-stem formation.
upaṭṭhahituṃ.translation_1: “To attend to you in your sickness, venerable sir.”

nañhi.meaning_2: for not; indeed not; because not
nañhi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of na + hi. In the text: "Piyā nañhi viyogavasena ..." = "for not seeing the dear ...".
nañhi.example_1: Piyā nañhi viyogavasena adassanaṃ appiyānañca upasaṅkamanavasena dassanaṃ nāma dukkhaṃ.
nañhi.translation_1: Because not seeing the dear due to separation, and seeing the unpleasant due to being in their presence, is indeed suffering.

ghanakoṭṭimaṃ.meaning_2: solid; cast; without a hollow; beaten solid
ghanakoṭṭimaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Used of a solid gold image (itthirūpa) made by goldsmiths. Compound of ghana (solid) + koṭṭima (from koṭṭeti, beaten/beaten work). Accusative singular agreeing with itthirūpaṃ here.
ghanakoṭṭimaṃ.example_1: So vayappatto mātāpitūhi,‘‘ tāta, āvāhaṃ te karissāmā ’’ ti vutte ‘‘ na me itthiyā attho ’’ ti paṭikkhipitvā punappunaṃ yāciyamāno pañcasate suvaṇṇakāre pakkosāpetvā rattasuvaṇṇanikkhasahassaṃ dāpetvā ativiya pāsādikaṃ ghanakoṭṭimaṃ itthirūpaṃ kāretvā puna mātāpitūhi,‘‘ tāta, tayi āvāhaṃ akaronte kulavaṃso na patiṭṭhahissati, kumārikaṃ te ānessāmā ’’ ti vutte ‘‘ tena hi sace me evarūpaṃ kumārikaṃ ānessatha, karissāmi vo vacanan ’’ ti taṃ suvaṇṇarūpakaṃ dasseti.
ghanakoṭṭimaṃ.translation_1: When he reached adulthood, his mother and father said, “Dear son, we will arrange a marriage for you,” and when told this, he rejected it saying, “I have no use for a woman,” but being asked again and again, he summoned five hundred goldsmiths, gave them a thousand gold coins, and had them make an exceedingly beautiful, solid, beaten-gold image of a woman. When his mother and father said again, “Dear son, if you do not marry, the family line will not continue; we will bring you a maiden,” he replied, “Very well, if you bring me a maiden such as this, I will do your bidding,” and he showed them the golden image.

katapaṭisammodanā.meaning_2: having exchanged greetings (with); having returned the greeting
katapaṭisammodanā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound of kata + paṭisammodana; nominative plural agreeing with the subject 'they'. The related PEU entry gives an adjective analysis, but here it functions verbally with 'saddhiṃ'.
katapaṭisammodanā.example_1: Te brāhmaṇehi saddhiṃ katapaṭisammodanā dhītaraṃ otāretvā heṭṭhāpāsāde suvaṇṇarūpakassa santike ṭhapesuṃ.
katapaṭisammodanā.translation_1: Having exchanged greetings with the brahmins, they had the maiden descend and placed her on the ground floor of the palace beside the golden image.

sabbissariyaṃ.meaning_2: all authority; complete sovereignty; all wealth and power
sabbissariyaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Nominal compound of sabba + issariya. Nominative singular in the text.
sabbissariyaṃ.example_1: Nandiyassāpi mātāpitaro kālamakaṃsu, gehe sabbissariyaṃ tassāyeva ahosi.
sabbissariyaṃ.translation_1: Nandiya’s mother and father also passed away; all authority in the house became hers alone.

niguhitvā.meaning_2: having concealed; having hidden; having covered up
niguhitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in -tvā of nigūhati (ni + √guh). In the sentence it describes the nuns hiding their offence. The PEU split ni+guha+tvā agrees.
niguhitvā.example_1: Tāsupi tatheva niguhitvā theraṃ paṭibāhituṃ asakkontīsu ekā tāva āha –
niguhitvā.translation_1: Even there, they tried to conceal their deeds and, failing to put off the Elder, one of them said first:

tiṇaparighāsaṃ.meaning_2: leftover grass; scraps of grass; remains of grass (eaten as food)
tiṇaparighāsaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text, the object of bhutvā. Describes coarse grass eaten as leftovers, contrasted with ācāmakuṇḍaka.
tiṇaparighāsaṃ.translation_1: “You ate the scraps of grass, you ate the rice-powder gruel;

khaṭakhaṭātisaddaṃ.meaning_2: sound of 'khaṭa khaṭa'; clattering sound; noise of wooden shoes
khaṭakhaṭātisaddaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text. The word is an onomatopoeic compound; the text also has the variant khaṭakhaṭasadda.
khaṭakhaṭātisaddaṃ.example_1: Ekadivasañhi satthā veḷuvane viharanto tesaṃ chabbaggiyānaṃ ubhohi hatthehi yaṭṭhiyo gahetvā kaṭṭhapādukā āruyha piṭṭhipāsāṇe caṅkamantānaṃ khaṭakhaṭātisaddaṃ sutvā,‘‘ ānanda, kiṃ saddo nāmeso ’’ ti pucchitvā ‘‘ chabbaggiyānaṃ pādukā āruyha caṅkamantānaṃ khaṭakhaṭasaddo ’’ ti sutvā sikkhāpadaṃ paññāpetvā ‘‘ bhikkhunā nāma kāyādīni rakkhituṃ vaṭṭatī ’’ ti vatvā dhammaṃ desento imā gāthā abhāsi –
khaṭakhaṭātisaddaṃ.translation_1: For one day, while the Teacher was dwelling in the Bamboo Grove, he heard a clattering sound from the bhikkhus of the Group of Six, who were holding staffs in both hands and wearing wooden shoes while walking up and down on a rock slab. Having asked, “Ānanda, what is that noise?” and hearing the reply, “It is the clattering sound of the Group of Six bhikkhus wearing wooden shoes and walking up and down,” he laid down a training rule, and saying, “It is proper for a bhikkhu to guard his deeds and so forth,” he expounded the Dhamma and declared these verses —

okirituṃ.meaning_2: to scatter; to strew; to spread
okirituṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Infinitive in -tuṃ of okirati (ava + √kir). In the text it depends on vaṭṭati: 'it is suitable to scatter'.
okirituṃ.example_1: Punadivasepi taṃ ṭhānaṃ āgantvā bhikkhūsu cīvaraṃ pārupantesu ekassa cīvarakaṇṇaṃ bhūmiyaṃ patitvā paṃsumhi pavaṭṭamānaṃ disvā ‘‘ idha vālukaṃ okirituṃ vaṭṭatī ’’ ti cintetvā vālukaṃ āharitvā okiri.
okirituṃ.translation_1: The next day he came to that place, and as the monks were putting on their robes, he saw the edge of one monk’s robe fall to the ground and get dirty in the dust, so he thought, “It is proper to scatter sand here,” and brought sand and spread it.

lāludāyittheravatthu.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of a story in the Dhammapada commentary; the elder's name is Lāludāyi in the text heading but Lāḷudāyi in the sentence.
lāludāyittheravatthu.translation_2: The story of Elder Lāḷudāyi is the fourth.

lāludāyittheraṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text, the person the Buddha's teaching refers to (ārabbha). A compound of the monk's name Lāḷudāyī and thera. The printed form lāludāyitthera shows the doubling of the initial t of thera after the vowel; the underlying name is Lāḷudāyī.
lāludāyittheraṃ.example_1: Asajjhāyamalāti imaṃ dhammadesanaṃ satthā jetavane viharanto lāludāyittheraṃ ārabbha kathesi.
lāludāyittheraṃ.translation_1: The Teacher gave this Dhamma teaching, Asajjhāyamalā, while dwelling in Jeta's Grove, referring to Elder Lāḷudāyi.

lāludāyitthero.meaning_2: Elder Lāludāyī; the elder named Lāludāyī
lāludāyitthero.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A personal name. The compound is lāludāyī + thera. The stem is uncertain as it is a proper name; the nominative singular is lāludāyitthero.
lāludāyitthero.example_1: Tehi dhammassavanavelāya āgantvā,‘‘ bhante, no dhammaṃ kathethā ’’ ti vutte lāludāyitthero āsane nisīditvā cittabījaniṃ gahetvā cālento ekampi dhammapadaṃ adisvā ‘‘ ahaṃ sarabhaññaṃ bhaṇissāmi, añño dhammakathaṃ kathetū ’’ ti vatvā otari.
lāludāyitthero.translation_1: When the time came for them to listen to the Dhamma, they said, "Venerable sir, teach us the Dhamma," and Elder Lāḷudāyi sat on the seat, took a beautiful fan, waved it, and, not seeing a single word of Dhamma, said, "I will chant the sacred word; let another person teach the Dhamma," and stepped down.

bhaṇāpetvā.meaning_2: causes to speak; makes recite; has chanted; orders to say
bhaṇāpetvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive (bhaṇāpetvā) of the causative bhaṇāpeti; in the text 'having made (someone) recite'.
bhaṇāpetvā.example_1: Te aññena sarabhaññaṃ bhaṇāpetvā puna rattiṃ theraṃ ānayiṃsu.
bhaṇāpetvā.translation_1: They did not have another person chant the sacred word, but brought the Elder back again at night.

lāludāyī.meaning_2: name of a monk; the foolish Udāyī
lāludāyī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name of a monk, a compound with the derogatory prefix lālu- (stupid; foolish). Nominative singular in the text. The commentary credits him with jealousy of Sāriputta and Moggallāna.
lāludāyī.example_1: ‘‘ ajja lāludāyī sāriputtamoggallānānaṃ guṇakathāya pavattamānāya ussūyanto attano dhammakathikabhāvaṃ pakāsetvā manussehi sakkāraṃ katvā ‘ dhammaṃ suṇomā ’ ti vutte catukkhattuṃ āsane nisīditvā kathetabbayuttakaṃ kiñci apassanto ‘ tvaṃ amhākaṃ ayyehi sāriputtamoggallānattherehi saddhiṃ yugaggāhaṃ gaṇhāsī ’ ti leḍḍudaṇḍādīni gahetvā santajjetvā palāpiyamāno vaccakuṭiyā patito ’’ ti.
lāludāyī.translation_1: "Today, while the discussion of the virtues of Sāriputta and Moggallāna was ongoing, Lāḷudāyi grew jealous, declared himself a Dhamma teacher, and when the people honored him and said, 'We will listen to the Dhamma,' he sat on the seat four times, saw not a single word suitable for teaching, and when we threatened him, saying, 'You compare yourself to our masters Sāriputta and Moggallāna,' he fell into a cesspool while fleeing."

lāludāyīti.meaning_2: Lāḷudāyī; the foolish Udāyī; name of a monk
lāludāyīti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text the word is followed by the quotation particle -ti (lāludāyīti = lāludāyī + iti). The first part is lāla, 'foolish, stupid'; the compound is a derogatory name for the monk Udāyī.
lāludāyīti.example_1: Tadā sīho sāriputto ahosi, sūkaro lāludāyīti.
lāludāyīti.translation_1: At that time, the lion was Sāriputta, and the pig was Lāḷudāyi.

lāludāyinā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Instrumental singular lāludāyinā (by Lāḷudāyī) in the text. Name of a monk; lāla means foolish.
lāludāyinā.example_1: Satthā imaṃ dhammadesanaṃ āharitvā,‘‘ bhikkhave, lāludāyinā appamattakova dhammo uggahito, sajjhāyaṃ pana neva akāsi, kiñci pariyattiṃ uggahetvā tassā asajjhāyakaraṇaṃ malamevā ’’ ti vatvā imaṃ gāthamāha –
lāludāyinā.translation_1: After bringing forth this Dhamma teaching, the Teacher said, "Bhikkhus, Lāḷudāyi learned only a little bit of Dhamma, but did not perform the recitation; to have learned some teaching and yet not to recite it is indeed an impurity," and spoke this verse—

jīvatuṃ.meaning_2: to live; to subsist; to make a living
jīvatuṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Infinitive of jīvati, used with sakkā ("it is possible to live"). The form is jīvituṃ in many editions; jīvatuṃ here is a variant spelling.
jīvatuṃ.example_1: Evarūpena hi amātarameva ‘‘ mātā me ’’ ti apitādayo eva ca ‘‘ pitā me ’’ tiādinā nayena vatvā ekavīsatividhāya anesanāya patiṭṭhāya sukhena jīvatuṃ sakkā.
jīvatuṃ.translation_1: For a person of such character, it is possible to live easily by establishing themselves in the twenty-one improper livelihoods, saying to one who is not a mother, "You are my mother," and to one who is not a father, "You are my father."

yakkhagahaajagaragahakumbhilagahādayo.meaning_2: fetters (seizures) by spirits, pythons, and crocodiles and so on
yakkhagahaajagaragahakumbhilagahādayo.construction: yakkha + gaha + ajagara + gaha + kumbhila + gaha + ādayo
yakkhagahaajagaragahakumbhilagahādayo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A long compound; nominative plural in the text. yakkhagaha = possession by a spirit, ajagaragaha = constriction by a python, kumbhilagaha = seizing by a crocodile.
yakkhagahaajagaragahakumbhilagahādayo.example_1: Dosasamoti yakkhagahaajagaragahakumbhilagahādayo ekasmiṃyeva attabhāve gaṇhituṃ sakkonti, dosagaho pana sabbattha ekantameva gaṇhātīti dosena samo gaho nāma natthi.
yakkhagahaajagaragahakumbhilagahādayo.translation_1: ‘No fetter like ill will’ means that while fetters like yakṣa-fetters, python-fetters, and crocodile-fetters can catch only in one body, the fetter of ill will catches everything absolutely. Therefore, there is no fetter like ill will.

mināpetvā.meaning_2: causes to measure; has measured out
mināpetvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in the text (mināpetvā), from the causative of √mā. The form mināpeti is the causative present 3rd singular.
mināpetvā.example_1: Athassa bhariyā sabbālaṅkārehi alaṅkaritvā mahājanassa passantasseva taṇḍule mināpetvā tehi bhattaṃ pacāpetvā dvārakoṭṭhake paññattāsane nisīditvā suvaṇṇakaṭacchuṃ ādāya ‘‘ bhattena atthikā āgacchantū ’’ ti ghosāpetvā āgatāgatānaṃ upanītabhājanāni pūretvā adāsi.
mināpetvā.translation_1: Then his wife, adorned with all her ornaments, measured out a pint-pot of rice before the eyes of the multitude, had it boiled, and sitting at the gate on a prepared seat, took a golden ladle and proclaimed, 'Let those who need rice come!' And she filled all the vessels brought to her by those who came.

nīhaṭamalo.meaning_2: whose impurity has been removed; with stains removed; free from defilement
nīhaṭamalo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it explains vantamala as maggañāṇena nīhaṭamala, "whose impurity is removed by the knowledge of the path". Partly a bahubbīhi compound, used of a person.
nīhaṭamalo.translation_1: Vantamalo means one whose impurities have been removed by the knowledge of the path.

kotuhale.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of kotūhala. In the text it is locative singular in the phrase ativiya kotuhale uppanne, 'when great excitement arose'. The root analysis is uncertain.
kotuhale.example_1: So dutiyadivase tatheva katvā tatiyadivase tesaṃ ativiya kotuhale uppanne mahātheraṃ upasaṅkamitvā,‘‘ bhante, kiñci vattabbaṃ atthi, tumhākaṃ pana santike vattuṃ na visahāmī ’’ ti vatvā therena ‘‘ hotu, āvuso, kathehī ’’ ti nippīḷito āha –
kotuhale.translation_1: He did the same on the second day; on the third day, when there was great agitation, he approached the senior elder and said, “Venerable sir, there is something that should be said, but I do not dare say it in your presence.” When pressed by the elder saying, “Never mind, friend, speak,” he said –

saṃbhogoti.meaning_2: eating together; sharing food; communal meal
saṃbhogoti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The -ti on the end is the quotative particle; the entry is for the main word. Probably nominative singular in the text. PEU connects it with √bhuj 1 but the compound analysis saṃ + bhoga is given here.

saṃbhogaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Used with saddhiṃ in the sense of associating (with). Accusative singular in the text.
saṃbhogaṃ.example_1: ‘‘ sappurisa, tvaṃ kulaputto, ayaṃ mahāthero lajjī pesaloti etena saddhiṃ saṃbhogaṃ karonto upaparikkhitvā kareyyāsī ’’ ti evamesa maṃ āgatadivasato paṭṭhāya vadatīti.
saṃbhogaṃ.translation_1: ‘Good man, you are a clansman, this senior elder is modest and virtuous, so investigate before you associate with him,’ and he has been saying this to me ever since the day I arrived.”
saṃbhogaṃ.example_2: ‘ mahātherena saddhiṃ saṃbhogaṃ mā akāsī ’’’ ti.
saṃbhogaṃ.translation_2: ‘Do not associate with the senior elder.’”

saṃbhogamakāsīti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Form in the text is saṃbhogaṃ + akāsi + iti: 'made shared enjoyment' (accusative singular), with akāsīti resolved as akāsi + iti.

anupādiṇṇakepi.meaning_2: not clung to; not attached; inanimate; without life
anupādiṇṇakepi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative singular in the text, in the phrase anupādiṇṇakepi. Contrasted with upādiṇṇaka (animate).
anupādiṇṇakepi.example_1: So jhānā vuṭṭhāya taṃ oloketvā ‘‘ kiṃ nu kho imaṃ padumaṃ jarāya pahaṭaṃ paññāyati, anupādiṇṇakepi evaṃ jarāya abhibhuyyamāne upādiṇṇake kathāva natthi.
anupādiṇṇakepi.translation_1: Rising from absorption and looking at it, he thought, “Why does this lotus appear to be struck by old age? If even things without life are overpowered by old age, there is no need to speak of things that have life.

parimilātāni.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Neuter nominative plural agreeing with kumudāni; contrasted with the fresh, dripping lilies in the water.
parimilātāni.example_1: Athassa jale kumudāni abhirūpāni udakapaggharantāni viya upaṭṭhahiṃsu, itarāni aggaggesu parimilātāni.
parimilātāni.translation_1: The water lilies in the water appeared beautiful and dripping with water, while the others were withered at the tips.

pākaṭībhūtaṃ.meaning_2: become manifest; become clear; become evident
pākaṭībhūtaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound of pākaṭī (adverb, 'clearly') + bhūta (pp of bhavati). Nt nominative singular agreeing with kammaṭṭhāna. The commentary glosses pākaṭībhūtāti pātubhūtā.
pākaṭībhūtaṃ.example_1: Satthā ‘‘ pākaṭībhūtaṃ idāni imassa bhikkhuno kammaṭṭhānan ’’ ti ñatvā gandhakuṭiyaṃ nisinnakova obhāsaṃ muñci, so tassa mukhaṃ pahari.
pākaṭībhūtaṃ.translation_1: Knowing that the monk’s meditation subject had now become manifest, the Teacher, sitting in the Perfumed Chamber, emitted a radiance that struck his face.

abhiruhaṇatthāya.meaning_2: to ascend; to board; to mount
abhiruhaṇatthāya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Infinitive expressing purpose: 'for the sake of boarding', used in the text with nāvaṃ (their boats); dative of abhiruhaṇa + atthāya, equivalent to abhiruhituṃ. Note √ruh 'ascend, grow'.
abhiruhaṇatthāya.example_1: Te suvaṇṇarajatamaṇimayā nāvāyo māpetvā suvaṇṇarajatamaṇimaye pallaṅke paññāpetvā pañcavaṇṇapadumasañchannaṃ udakaṃ karitvā,‘‘ bhante, amhākampi anuggahaṃ karothā ’’ ti attano attano nāvaṃ abhiruhaṇatthāya satthāraṃ yāciṃsu.
abhiruhaṇatthāya.translation_1: They created boats made of gold, silver, and jewels, prepared couches made of gold, silver, and jewels, made the water covered with five-colored lotuses, and requested the Teacher to mount their respective boats, saying, “Venerable sir, be favorable to us too.”

gaṅgorohaṇasamāgamoti.meaning_2: assembly on the occasion of the ascent from the Ganges; gathering at the descent from the Ganges
gaṅgorohaṇasamāgamoti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi gaṅgā + orohaṇa > gaṅgorohaṇa. The -ti at the end is the quotation particle iti (gaṅgorohaṇasamāgamo + iti), not part of the word. Nominative singular in the text, naming the third of three great assemblies.
gaṅgorohaṇasamāgamoti.example_1: Tayo eva kira samāgamā mahantā ahesuṃ – yamakapāṭihāriyasamāgamo devorohaṇasamāgamo ayaṃ gaṅgorohaṇasamāgamoti.
gaṅgorohaṇasamāgamoti.translation_1: Tradition has it that only these three assemblies were so great: the assembly on the occasion of the Twin Miracle, the assembly on the occasion of the descent of the devas, and this assembly on the occasion of the ascent from the Ganges.

kukkuṭaaṇḍakhādikāvatthu.meaning_2: story about a woman who ate chicken eggs
kukkuṭaaṇḍakhādikāvatthu.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of a story in the Dhammapada commentary; neuter, nominative singular. khādikā is a feminine agent noun from √khād; vatthu here means 'story, case'.
kukkuṭaaṇḍakhādikāvatthu.translation_1: 2. The Story about a Woman Who Ate Chicken Eggs
kukkuṭaaṇḍakhādikāvatthu.translation_2: The second is the Story about a Woman Who Ate Chicken Eggs.

kukkuṭaaṇḍakhādikaṃ.meaning_2: one who eats chicken eggs; egg-eater (of a hen)
kukkuṭaaṇḍakhādikaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Describes a hen that eats its own eggs. Accusative singular in the text, qualifying a fowl (the commentary explains it as a hen).
kukkuṭaaṇḍakhādikaṃ.example_1: Paradukkhūpadhānenāti imaṃ dhammadesanaṃ satthā jetavane viharanto ekaṃ kukkuṭaaṇḍakhādikaṃ ārabbha kathesi.
kukkuṭaaṇḍakhādikaṃ.translation_1: The Teacher, while dwelling at Jeta’s Grove, related this exposition of the Dhamma, ‘By causing affliction to others,’ with reference to a woman who ate chicken eggs.

paṇḍuraṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text paṇḍuraṃ is part of the place name paṇḍuraṃ nāma, apparently a village (gāma); nominative/accusative singular neuter or masculine form functioning as a name.
paṇḍuraṃ.example_1: Sāvatthiyā kira avidūre paṇḍuraṃ nāma eko gāmo, tattheko kevaṭṭo vasati.
paṇḍuraṃ.translation_1: They say that not far from Sāvatthī there was a certain village named Paṇḍupura, and a certain fisherman lived there.

raṭṭhadisattā.meaning_2: resembling a kingdom; like a kingdom; having the appearance of a realm
raṭṭhadisattā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of raṭṭha and disattā (resembling, looking like). Agrees with dvādasāyatanāni in the quote; nominative plural neuter.
raṭṭhadisattā.translation_1: The twelve sense bases are called ‘kingdom’ because they are vast, resembling a kingdom.

svākhāto.meaning_2: well proclaimed; well taught; well expounded
svākhāto.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text svākhāto agrees with dhammo (nominative singular masculine). The PED treats it as a compound of su + akkhāta; su becomes sv before a vowel. Variant svākhāto, the sandhi form of su + akkhāta.
svākhāto.example_1: Dhammagatā satīti ‘‘ svākhāto bhagavatā dhammo ’’ tiādippabhede dhammaguṇe ārabbha uppajjamānā sati.
svākhāto.translation_1: ‘Mindfulness directed to the Dhamma’: mindfulness that arises based upon the Dhamma-virtues such as ‘The Dhamma is well-proclaimed by the Blessed One’.

kosmi.meaning_2: who am I?; who am I
kosmi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of ko (who?) + asmi (am I), in the phrase 'kosi tvaṃ, kosmi ahaṃ' ('who are you? who am I?'). Sometimes written kosmi ahaṃ with ahaṃ as a separate word.
kosmi.example_1: Dukkho samānasaṃvāsoti gihino vā hi ye jātigottakulabhogehi pabbajitā vā sīlācārabāhusaccādīhi samānāpi hutvā ‘‘ kosi tvaṃ, kosmi ahan ’’ tiādīni vatvā adhikaraṇapasutā honti, te asamānā nāma, tehi saddhiṃ saṃvāso dukkhoti attho.
kosmi.translation_1: ‘Living with those unlike oneself is painful’: whether they are householders or gone-forth, even if they are equal in terms of birth, clan, or wealth, or equal in terms of virtue, conduct, and learning, if they are devoted to disputes saying ‘Who are you? Who am I?’, they are not ‘like’ one another; living with them is painful—this is the meaning.

sabbīriyāpathesu.meaning_2: all postures; every mode of deportment
sabbīriyāpathesu.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative plural in the text. The compound is used in a stock description of a meditator who is unattached in all four postures (walking, standing, sitting, lying down).
sabbīriyāpathesu.example_1: Atanditoti jaṅghabalaṃ nissāya jīvitakappanena akusīto hutvā sabbīriyāpathesu ekakova carantoti attho.
sabbīriyāpathesu.translation_1: 'Untiring' (atandito) means not being lazy in maintaining one's life by relying on the strength of one's legs, and walking alone in all postures, is the meaning.

ramāpetvā.meaning_2: having caused to enjoy; having given pleasure (to); having made delightful
ramāpetvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative absolutive of ramāpeti (caus of ramati). In the text used of Sundarī's claim that she had given Gotama his fill of sensual pleasure; grammatically feminine subject (-āmhī), but the form is absolute.
ramāpetvā.example_1: Sā taṃ sutvā ‘‘ sādhū ’’ ti sampaṭicchitvā pakkantā tato paṭṭhāya mālāgandhavilepanakappūrakaṭukaphalādīni gahetvā sāyaṃ mahājanassa satthu dhammadesanaṃ sutvā nagaraṃ pavisanakāle jetavanābhimukhī gacchati,‘‘ kahaṃ gacchasī ’’ ti ca puṭṭhā ‘‘ samaṇassa gotamassa santikaṃ gamissāmi, ahañhi tena saddhiṃ ekagandhakuṭiyaṃ vasāmī ’’ ti vatvā aññatarasmiṃ titthiyārāme vasitvā pātova jetavanamaggaṃ otaritvā nagarābhimukhī āgacchantī ‘‘ kiṃ, sundari, kahaṃ gatāsī ’’ ti puṭṭhā ‘‘ samaṇena gotamena saddhiṃ ekagandhakuṭiyaṃ vasitvā taṃ kilesaratiyā ramāpetvā āgatāmhī ’’ ti vadati.
ramāpetvā.translation_1: Hearing this, she agreed, saying, 'Very well,' and departed. From that time on, taking garlands, perfumes, ointments, camphor, bitter fruits, and so on, she would go towards Jetavana in the evening when the people were returning to the city after listening to the Teacher's Dhamma talk. When asked, 'Where are you going?' she would reply, 'I am going to the ascetic Gotama's presence, for I live with him in the Perfumed Chamber.' Then she would stay in some sectarians' monastery and early the next morning descend onto the road to Jetavana and come towards the city. When asked, 'Sundarī, where have you been?' she would reply, 'I stayed with the ascetic Gotama in the Perfumed Chamber, and after having permitted him to take his fill of pleasure, I have returned.'

olīyitvā.meaning_2: having held back; having been slack; having lingered (over); having done sluggishly
olīyitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive of olīyati; in the text it explains sithila: acting slackly, holding back from effort. Sandhi with the following karaṇena is not part of the word.
olīyitvā.example_1: Sithilanti olīyitvā karaṇena sithilagāhaṃ katvā kataṃ yaṃkiñci kammaṃ.
olīyitvā.translation_1: Sithilan (loose) refers to any deed done by holding it loosely or acting lazily.

avattasamādāno.meaning_2: without unsteady undertaking; with firm commitment; not wavering in one's undertaking
avattasamādāno.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Bahuvrīhi compound: na + vatta (shaky, unstable) + samādāna (undertaking); nominative singular, agreeing with the subject in the text, glossed there as thirakatameva katvā.
avattasamādāno.example_1: Daḷhamenaṃ parakkameti thirakatameva katvā avattasamādāno hutvā enaṃ kayirā.
avattasamādāno.translation_1: Daḷhamenaṃ parakkame (one should struggle with it steadfastly) means: one should do it having made it something firmly established, and without shaky commitment, one should do it.

gopayituṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Infinitive gopayituṃ in the text, from the causative base gopaya; related causative gopeti. The PEU analysis (Gupa+ṇaya+tu) points to the same causative formation.
gopayituṃ.example_1: Tasmā aphāsukaṃ vassaṃ vasimhā ’’ ti vutte ‘‘ alaṃ, bhikkhave, mā cintayittha, phāsuvihāro nāma niccakālaṃ dullabho, bhikkhunā nāma yathā te manussā nagaraṃ gopayiṃsu, evaṃ attabhāvameva gopayituṃ vaṭṭatī ’’ ti vatvā imaṃ gāthamāha –
gopayituṃ.translation_1: Therefore, we did not spend the Rains Retreat pleasantly.” When they had said this, he replied, “Enough, bhikkhus, do not worry. Comfortable living is always rare. It is fitting for a bhikkhu to guard his own being, just as those people guarded their town.” Having said this, he spoke this verse:

nibbānadisaṃ.meaning_2: direction of Nibbāna; region of Nibbāna; the destination of Nibbāna
nibbānadisaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The final ā of disā is shortened before the case ending; accusative singular in the text. The PEU reads it as thī (feminine).
nibbānadisaṃ.example_1: Tassattho – yāni tāni hatthiyānādīni yānāni, na hi etehi yānehi koci puggalo supinantenapi agatapubbattā ‘‘ agatan ’’ ti saṅkhātaṃ nibbānadisaṃ tathā gaccheyya, yathā pubbabhāge indriyadamena aparabhāge ariyamaggabhāvanāya sudantena danto nibbisevano sappañño puggalo taṃ agatapubbaṃ disaṃ gacchati, dantabhūmiṃ pāpuṇāti.
nibbānadisaṃ.translation_1: The meaning: those vehicles—elephant vehicles and so on—are not vehicles by which any person could reach the destination known as 'the destination beyond,' the destination of Nirvana—not even in a dream, because it is a place not previously visited. But the wise person, tamed by the training of the faculties in the beginning and by the cultivation of the Noble Path in the end, tamed, goes to that place not previously visited—he attains the level of the tamed, having himself been tamed.

āharahatthakaalaṃsāṭakatatravaṭṭakakākam.meaning_2: of Āharahatthaka, Alaṃsāṭaka, Tattavaṭṭaka, Kākamāsaka and Bhuttavamitaka (brahmins)
āharahatthakaalaṃsāṭakatatravaṭṭakakākam.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A string of five brahmin names in the genitive plural, with sandhi ā + a > ā at each junction; the whole compound is glossed by aññataro in the text.
āharahatthakaalaṃsāṭakatatravaṭṭakakākam.translation_1: “Gluttonous” (mahagghaso) means a big eater, like one of the brahmins known as Āharahatthaka, Alaṃsāṭaka, Tattavaṭṭaka, Kākamāsaka, or Bhuttavamitaka.

kiliṭṭhanivāsanapārupano.meaning_2: wearing dirty robes; having soiled inner and outer garments
kiliṭṭhanivāsanapārupano.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Descriptive compound of the novice's appearance; nominative singular in the text. PEU splits it as kiliṭṭha + nivāsanapārupāna.
kiliṭṭhanivāsanapārupano.example_1: Atha kho sāmaṇero vuḍḍhimanvāya paripakkindriyo anabhiratiyā pīḷito anabhiratiṃ vinodetuṃ asakkonto paruḷhakesanakho kiliṭṭhanivāsanapārupano kassaci anārocetvā pattacīvaramādāya ekakova mātugharaṃ agamāsi.
kiliṭṭhanivāsanapārupano.translation_1: Then, when the novice reached maturity with fully developed faculties, he was oppressed by dissatisfaction, and unable to dispel it, with hair and nails grown long, and robes dirty and soiled, he took his bowl and robe and, without telling anyone, went all alone to his mother’s house.

aniggaṇhantassa.meaning_2: not restraining; not controlling; not subduing
aniggaṇhantassa.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Genitive singular (agreeing with cittaṃ as object of the restraining) in aniggaṇhantassa; the verb is na + niggaṇhāti. The negated participle is used of one who does not restrain the mind.
aniggaṇhantassa.example_1: Athassa acirūpasampannassa satthā cittaniggahe ussāhaṃ janento ‘‘ cittaṃ nāmetaṃ nānārammaṇesu dīgharattaṃ cārikaṃ carantaṃ aniggaṇhantassa sotthibhāvo nāma natthi, tasmā aṅkusena mattahatthino viya cittassa niggaṇhane yogo karaṇīyo ’’ ti vatvā imaṃ gāthamāha –
aniggaṇhantassa.translation_1: Then, for him who had but recently received the higher ordination, the Teacher, wishing to arouse effort in subduing the mind, said, “For one who does not restrain this mind, which wanders for a long time among various objects, there is no safety; therefore, one should apply effort in restraining the mind, like an elephant-driver with his hook,” and spoke this verse—

sādhinī.meaning_2: name of the mother of the two brothers
sādhinī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name of a woman. Nominative singular in the text. Possibly a feminine form of sādhana or a variant reading of Sādhinī/Sādhanī; the link to a root is uncertain.
sādhinī.example_1: Mātā pana nesaṃ sādhinī nāma, kaniṭṭhabhaginī tāpanā nāma.
sādhinī.translation_1: Their mother was named Sādhinī, and their younger sister was named Tāpanā.
sādhinī.example_2: ‘‘ Mātā pana te sādhinī kahan ’’ ti?

saṃsibbantī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Present participle feminine nominative singular saṃsibbantī agreeing with māluvālatā; glossed by pariyonandhantī.
saṃsibbantī.example_1: Yathā pana rukkhaṃ saṃsibbantī pariyonandhantī tassa vināsāya māluvālatā vaḍḍhati, evamassa cha dvārāni nissāya punappunaṃ uppajjanato taṇhā vaḍḍhatīti attho.
saṃsibbantī.translation_1: Just as a parasitic vine that sews together and wraps around a tree grows for its destruction, so, too, craving grows for that person because it arises again and again due to the six sense doors; this is the meaning.

pariyonandhantī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Present 3rd singular feminine agreeing with māluvālatā; further sandhi from pariyonandhati. Also possible analysis pari + upa + √nah.
pariyonandhantī.example_1: Yathā pana rukkhaṃ saṃsibbantī pariyonandhantī tassa vināsāya māluvālatā vaḍḍhati, evamassa cha dvārāni nissāya punappunaṃ uppajjanato taṇhā vaḍḍhatīti attho.
pariyonandhantī.translation_1: Just as a parasitic vine that sews together and wraps around a tree grows for its destruction, so, too, craving grows for that person because it arises again and again due to the six sense doors; this is the meaning.

ālulamānā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Feminine nominative singular agreeing with the rebirth-bound being; perhaps confused with ākulamāna. The root √lul is not in the given list.
ālulamānā.example_1: Tato cavitvā puna gativasena ālulamānā idāni sūkarayoniyaṃ nibbatti, idaṃ kāraṇaṃ disvā mayā sitaṃ pātukatanti.
ālulamānā.translation_1: Passing from there, confused by the course of rebirth, she has now been reborn in the womb of a sow; having seen this reason, I displayed a smile.”

kāvīrapaṭṭane.meaning_2: Kāvīra Port; name of a port city
kāvīrapaṭṭane.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative singular in the text. Probably an ancient port on the west coast of India; the first element kāvīra is otherwise unknown.
kāvīrapaṭṭane.example_1: Sāpi kho sūkarapotikā tato cavitvā suvaṇṇabhūmiyaṃ rājakule nibbatti, tato cutā bārāṇasiyaṃ, tato cutā suppārakapaṭṭane assavāṇijagehe nibbatti, tato cutā kāvīrapaṭṭane nāvikassa gehe nibbatti, tato cutā anurādhapure issarakulagehe nibbatti, tato cutā tasseva dakkhiṇadisāya bhokkantagāme sumanassa nāma kuṭumbikassa dhītā nāmena sumanā eva hutvā nibbatti.
kāvīrapaṭṭane.translation_1: That young sow, passing from that state of existence, was reborn in Suvaṇṇabhūmi in the royal household; passing from that state, she was reborn at Benares; passing from that state, she was reborn at Suppāraka Port in the household of a horse-dealer; passing from that state, she was reborn at Kāvīra Port in the household of a mariner; passing from that state, she was reborn in Anurādhapura in the household of a nobleman; passing from that state, she was reborn in the Southern District in the village of Bhokkanta as the daughter of a householder named Sumana, being named Sumanā after him.

lakuṇḍakaatimbaro.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of lakuṇḍaka-atimbara, the name of a minister of King Duṭṭhagāmaṇī; nominative singular in the text.
lakuṇḍakaatimbaro.example_1: Tattha naṃ duṭṭhagāmaṇirañño amacco lakuṇḍakaatimbaro nāma kenacideva karaṇīyena gato disvā mahantaṃ maṅgalaṃ katvā ādāya mahāpuṇṇagāmaṃ gato.
lakuṇḍakaatimbaro.translation_1: There, a minister of King Duṭṭhagāmaṇī named Lakuṇṭaka Atimbara, having gone on some business or other, saw her, married her with great pomp, and took her with him to the village of Mahāpuṇṇa.

lakuṇḍakaatimbaramahāmattassa.meaning_2: the great minister Lakuṇḍaka Atimbara; the chief minister Lakuṇḍaka Atimbara
lakuṇḍakaatimbaramahāmattassa.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Genitive singular in the text, referring to a minister whose wife was reborn as a sow. The name may be Lakuṇḍaka Atimbara; alternative spelling Lakuṇṭaka.
lakuṇḍakaatimbaramahāmattassa.example_1: Atha naṃ koṭipabbatamahāvihāravāsī mahāanuruddhatthero nāma tattha piṇḍāya caritvā tassā gehadvāre ṭhito disvā bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ kathesi,‘‘ āvuso, sūkarapotikā nāma lakuṇḍakaatimbaramahāmattassa bhariyabhāvaṃ pattā, aho acchariyan ’’ ti.
lakuṇḍakaatimbaramahāmattassa.translation_1: Then, Elder Mahāanuruddha, who lived in the great monastery of Koṭipabbata, went to that village for alms and, standing at her door, saw her and said to the bhikkhus, 'Friends, it is a wonder that a young sow has attained the state of being the wife of the great minister Lakuṇṭaka Atimbara! How amazing!'

kāvīrapaṭṭanaṃ.meaning_2: Kāvīra Port; the port named Kāvīra
kāvīrapaṭṭanaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Place name in a list of former rebirths in the Dhammapada commentary. Accusative singular in the text.
kāvīrapaṭṭanaṃ.example_1: Sā parinibbānadivase bhikkhubhikkhunīhi pucchitā bhikkhunisaṅghassa sabbaṃ imaṃ pavattiṃ nirantaraṃ kathetvā sannipatitassa bhikkhusaṅghassa majjhe maṇḍalārāmavāsinā dhammapadabhāṇakamahātissattherena saddhiṃ saṃsanditvā ‘‘ ahaṃ pubbe manussayoniyaṃ nibbattitvā tato cutā kukkuṭī hutvā tattha senassa santikā sīsacchedaṃ patvā rājagahe nibbattā, paribbājikāsu pabbajitvā paṭhamajjhānabhūmiyaṃ nibbattitvā tato cutā seṭṭhikule nibbattā nacirasseva cavitvā sūkarayoniṃ gantvā tato cutā suvaṇṇabhūmiṃ, tato cutā bārāṇasiṃ, tato cutā suppārakapaṭṭanaṃ, tato cutā kāvīrapaṭṭanaṃ, tato cutā anurādhapuraṃ, tato cutā bhokkantagāman ’’ ti evaṃ samavisame terasa attabhāve patvā ‘‘ idāni ukkaṇṭhitvā pabbajitvā arahattaṃ pattā, sabbepi appamādena sampādethā ’’ ti vatvā catasso parisā saṃvejetvā parinibbāyīti.
