kāvīrapaṭṭanaṃ.translation_1: On the day of her Parinibbāna, being asked by the bhikkhus and bhikkhunī, she related her entire history without interruption to the bhikkhunī-sangha, and in the midst of the gathered bhikkhus, joining the account with Mahātissa the Elder of Maṇḍalārāma who was a reciter of the Dhammapada, she said, 'I previously, having been born in the human realm, passed away and became a young chicken; in that life, I was beheaded by a hawk and reborn at Rājagaha. I went forth among the wanderers, attained the first jhāna, passed away, and was reborn in the world of Brahma; passing from there, I was reborn in a merchant’s household; not long after, I passed away and went to the womb of a sow; passing from that state, I went to Suvaṇṇabhūmi; passing from that, to Benares; passing from that, to Suppāraka Port; passing from that, to Kāvīra Port; passing from that, to Anurādhapura; passing from that, to the village of Bhokkanta. Having reached thirteen such uneven states of existence, now, having become weary, I have gone forth and attained Arahantship. Do you all also complete your work with diligence!' So saying, and having inspired awe in the four assemblies, she attained Parinibbāna.

dummociyaṃ.meaning_2: hard to be freed; difficult to escape; hard to untie
dummociyaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is part of the gloss of duppamuñcaṃ, nominative singular neuter agreeing with kilesabandhanaṃ. Spelling with -iya- rather than -anīya- is unusual; the PEU suggests du+muca+ṇaya+kha, i.e. a secondary derivation from the root muc.
dummociyaṃ.example_1: Duppamuñcanti lobhavasena hi ekavārampi uppannaṃ kilesabandhanaṃ daṭṭhaṭṭhānato kacchapo viya dummociyaṃ hotīti duppamuñcaṃ.
dummociyaṃ.translation_1: Duppamuñcaṃ means that, indeed, because of greed, the bond of defilements arises, and it is difficult to be freed from, like a turtle caught in a trap.

laṅghikadhītā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text the subject of the sentence; nominative singular. Daughter of a pole-acrobat or gymnast (laṅghika).
laṅghikadhītā.example_1: Athekā laṅghikadhītā vaṃsaṃ abhiruyha tassa upari parivattitvā tassa pariyante ākāse caṅkamamānā naccati ceva gāyati ca.
laṅghikadhītā.translation_1: At that time, a certain daughter of an acrobat climbed a pole, turned somersaults atop it, and while walking on the air at the tip of that pole, danced and sang.

cuddasakkhattuṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Adverbial compound used with parivattitvā to mean turning fourteen times in the air.
cuddasakkhattuṃ.example_1: Evañca pana vatvā vaṃsamatthakato vehāsaṃ abbhuggantvā ākāseva cuddasakkhattuṃ parivattitvā oruyha vaṃsamatthakeva aṭṭhāsi.
cuddasakkhattuṃ.translation_1: And having said this, he sprang from the pole-tip into the sky, turned fourteen somersaults in the air, landed, and stood back on the tip of the pole.

nayīdha.meaning_2: there is no here; not here
nayīdha.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Na + idha contracted to nayīdha; the vowel of na is lengthened before the enclitic. Occurs in the Dhammapada commentary verse.
nayīdha.example_1: Nayīdha naccaṃ vā gītaṃ vā, tāḷaṃ vā susamāhitaṃ;
nayīdha.translation_1: there is no dance or song here, nor well-composed percussion;

nevābhinandi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of na eva + abhinandi (√nand, aorist). Together with na paṭikkosi: 'neither approved nor rejected'. Indeclinable na + eva.
nevābhinandi.example_1: Desanāvasāne upako ājīvako tathāgatassa vacanaṃ nevābhinandi, na paṭikkosi.
nevābhinandi.translation_1: At the end of the teaching, the Ājīvaka Upaka neither expressed approval of the Tathāgata’s words, nor opposed them.

abhiharāpetvā.meaning_2: having caused to be brought; having had (the wealth) conveyed (to)
abhiharāpetvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative absolutive of abhiharāpeti; in the text it refers to the king having the dead miser's wealth brought into the royal palace.
abhiharāpetvā.example_1: Tassa kira kālakiriyaṃ sutvā rājā pasenadi kosalo ‘‘ aputtakaṃ sāpateyyaṃ kassa pāpuṇātī ’’ ti pucchitvā ‘‘ rañño ’’ ti sutvā sattahi divasehi tassa gehato dhanaṃ rājakulaṃ abhiharāpetvā satthu santikaṃ upasaṅkamitvā ‘‘ handa kuto nu tvaṃ, mahārāja, āgacchasi divādivassā ’’ ti vutte ‘‘ idha, bhante, sāvatthiyaṃ seṭṭhi, gahapati, kālakato, tamahaṃ aputtakaṃ sāpateyyaṃ rājantepuraṃ abhiharitvā āgacchāmī ’’ ti āha.
abhiharāpetvā.translation_1: It seems that upon hearing of his death, King Pasenadi Kosala inquired, “To whom does the wealth of one who dies childless fall?” Hearing the reply, “To the king,” he had the wealth removed from his house to the royal palace over seven days, then approached the Teacher. When the Teacher asked, “Now, Great King, where are you coming from in the middle of the day?” he replied, “Venerable sir, here in Sāvatthī a rich householder has died; I have been having his childless estate removed into the royal compound, and am just returning.”

sakiyāvadhī.meaning_2: he killed himself with his own (speech); he destroyed himself by his own words
sakiyāvadhī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi resolution: sakiyā + vadhī, i.e. sakiyāya vācāya vadhī. In sakiyāvadhī the instrumental ending of sakiyā(ya) is lost before v; compare the parallel line etena ... vācāya ... vadhī. Could alternatively be taken as an irregular compound sakiyā + vadhī; vadhī is 3rd sg aorist of vadhati.
sakiyāvadhī.translation_1: though he had a good grip on the stick, he killed himself with his own speech.”

vicintanatāya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Feminine abstract noun. Instrumental singular in the text, meaning 'by reflecting again and again'.
vicintanatāya.example_1: Tasseva dhammassa punappunaṃ vicintanatāya dhammaṃ anuvicintayaṃ , taṃ dhammaṃ āvajjento manasikarontoti attho.
vicintanatāya.translation_1: Dhammaṃ anuvicintayaṃ means pondering the Dhamma again and again because of its repeated contemplation; the meaning is that he considers and keeps that Dhamma in mind.

ayasaṅghāṭakāni.meaning_2: iron spike; iron harrow; iron implement
ayasaṅghāṭakāni.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text, the nominative plural form ayasaṅghāṭakāni is used with odahiṃsu, referring to iron spikes or iron instruments struck into the ground. The PEU suggests a connection with √han, but the compound is best treated as aya + saṅghāṭaka.
ayasaṅghāṭakāni.example_1: Tassānantarā mahantāni ayasaṅghāṭakāni nirantaraṃ bhūmiyaṃ odahiṃsu.
ayasaṅghāṭakāni.translation_1: Behind that, they had continuously hammered great iron spikes into the ground.

ayasaṅghāṭakānañca.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it appears as ayasaṅghāṭakānañca, with the diminutive suffix -ka and the enclitic -ca. Here it refers to a defensive iron device with spikes. The compound may be analysed as aya + saṅghāṭa.
ayasaṅghāṭakānañca.example_1: Iti imañcārakkhaṃ upāsikāya ca antogehe ṭhitabhāvaṃ paṭicca te corā okāsaṃ alabhantā taṃ divasaṃ tassā gatabhāvaṃ ñatvā umaṅgaṃ bhinditvā tipuparikhāya ca ayasaṅghāṭakānañca heṭṭhābhāgeneva gehaṃ pavisitvā corajeṭṭhakaṃ tassā santikaṃ pahiṇiṃsu ‘‘ sace sā amhākaṃ idha paviṭṭhabhāvaṃ sutvā nivattitvā gehābhimukhī āgacchati, asinā naṃ paharitvā mārethā ’’ ti.
ayasaṅghāṭakānañca.translation_1: Thus, relying on this protection and the fact that the lay follower was inside, the thieves could find no opportunity. On that day, knowing she had gone away, they dug a tunnel and, passing beneath the lead trench and the iron spikes, entered the house. Having entered, they sent the ringleader to the lay follower, saying, 'If she hears that we have entered and turns back towards the house, strike her with a sword and kill her.'

rajāpetvā.meaning_2: having caused to be dyed; having had (them) dyed
rajāpetvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative absolutive of rajati (to dye); here the Elder has the robes dyed with red clay before ordaining the men.
rajāpetvā.example_1: Thero ‘‘ sādhū ’’ ti vatvā tehi nivatthavatthānaṃ dasāni chindāpetvā tambamattikāya rajāpetvā te pabbājetvā sīlesu patiṭṭhāpesi.
rajāpetvā.translation_1: The Elder said 'Very well', and having had the borders of their worn garments cut off, had them dyed with red clay, ordained them, and established them in the precepts.

vavatthāpetvā.meaning_2: having determined; having defined; having appointed; having settled
vavatthāpetvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative absolutive of vavatthāpeti (caus of vavatthāti). In the sentence it means having defined or determined the teaching according to the monks' dispositions.
vavatthāpetvā.example_1: Satthā vīsayojanasatamatthake jetavanamahāvihāre nisinnova te bhikkhū oloketvā tesaṃ cariyavasena dhammadesanaṃ vavatthāpetvā obhāsaṃ pharitvā sammukhe nisīditvā kathento viya imā gāthā abhāsi –
vavatthāpetvā.translation_1: The Teacher, while dwelling in Jeta's Grove monastery 120 leagues away, looked at those monks, determined the Dhamma teaching according to their dispositions, suffused them with radiance, and as if sitting in their presence speaking to them, spoke these verses—

avaḷañjo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Describes a path (magga) that has become overgrown from disuse. Nominative singular in the text.
avaḷañjo.example_1: ‘‘ āvuso naṅgalatthera, tava vicaraṇamaggo avaḷañjo viya jāto, ācariyassa santikaṃ na gacchasi maññe ’’ ti.
avaḷañjo.translation_1: “Friend Naṅgalakula, your path for traveling seems to have become unused; I suppose you do not go to the presence of your teacher anymore.”

ogalitvā.example_1: So tikkhattuṃ nāgarājassa paṭiññaṃ gahetvā ākāse ṭhitakova dvādasayojanikaṃ brahmattabhāvaṃ māpetvā ākāsato oruyha nāgarājassa phaṇe akkamitvā adhomukhaṃ nippīḷesi, tāvadeva balavatā purisena akkantaallacammaṃ viya nāgarājassa phaṇe akkantamatte ogalitvā dabbimattā phaṇapuṭakā ahesuṃ.
ogalitvā.translation_1: Having obtained the Nāga king’s promise three times, the novice stood in the air, assumed the form of a Brahmā twelve leagues high, descended from the air, trod on the Nāga king’s hood, and squeezed him downward. Just as when a strong man treads on a damp hide, the moment he stepped on the Nāga king’s hood, the folds formed into the size of spoons.

sañcāletvā.meaning_2: having shaken; having made move; having agitated
sañcāletvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive of the causative sañcāleti (saṃ + √cal, caus). Used with gahetvā in the sentence: taking hold of the novice and shaking him.
sañcāletvā.example_1: Athekacce sāmaṇeraṃ sīsepi kaṇṇesupi bāhāyampi gahetvā sañcāletvā ‘‘ kiṃ, sāmaṇera cūḷakaniṭṭha, na ukkaṇṭhitosī ’’ ti āhaṃsu.
sañcāletvā.translation_1: Some took hold of the novice by the head, ears, or arms, shaking him, saying, “What is it, little novice, are you not discontented?”

ghanasuvaṇṇakoṭṭimesu.meaning_2: made of solid gold; covered with solid gold
ghanasuvaṇṇakoṭṭimesu.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative plural in the text, agreeing with senāsanakuṭesu. Could also be taken as an adjective meaning 'with solid-gold flooring'.
ghanasuvaṇṇakoṭṭimesu.example_1: So visākhāya kāritesu ghanasuvaṇṇakoṭṭimesu senāsanakuṭesu ekaṃ saṭṭhikuṭaudakagaṇhanakaṃ mahāghaṭaṃ hatthena gahetvā ‘‘ iminā me ukkhipitvā aṃsakūṭe ṭhapitena attho natthī ’’ ti olambakaṃ katvā vehāsaṃ abbhuggantvā himavantābhimukho pakkhandi.
ghanasuvaṇṇakoṭṭimesu.translation_1: He took a great golden waterpot of the monastery, which could hold sixty water-measures, made by Visākhā, and thinking, “I have no need to lift this and put it on my shoulder,” he held it by his hand, rose into the air, and set off toward the Himālaya region.

khīpitvāpi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Written khīpitvā before -pi. Absolutive from the causative khīpeti (to cause to sneeze), i.e. 'having sneezed'. Sā is feminine, the subject is a woman.
khīpitvāpi.example_1: Sā khīpitvāpi kāsitvāpi pakkhalitvāpi ‘‘ namo tassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassā ’’ ti imaṃ udānaṃ udānesi.
khīpitvāpi.translation_1: Whenever she sneezed, coughed, or stumbled, she would breathe forth this exclamation: “Reverence to the Blessed One, the Perfected One, the fully awakened Buddha!”

biliṅgakabhāradvājoti.meaning_2: Biliṅgaka Bhāradvāja (name of a brahmin, younger brother of the Buddha's disciples)
biliṅgakabhāradvājoti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name in the text, joined with the quotation particle -ti; nominative singular. Also spelled Bilaṅgika Bhāradvāja.
biliṅgakabhāradvājoti.example_1: Aparepissa sundarikabhāradvājo biliṅgakabhāradvājoti dve kaniṭṭhabhātaro satthāraṃ akkosantāva satthārā vinītā pabbajitvā arahattaṃ pāpuṇiṃsu.
biliṅgakabhāradvājoti.translation_1: His other two younger brothers, Sundarī Bhāradvāja and Bilaṅgika Bhāradvāja, also reviled the Teacher, but were trained by the Teacher, went forth, and attained arahantship.

pisāpetvā.meaning_2: having caused to be ground; having had (it) crushed; having made (someone) grind
pisāpetvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative absolutive of pisāpeti (from √pis 2, 'grind, crush'), with the -āpe- causative sign; the simplex would be pisitvā. In the sentence the merchant has the sandalwood ground by others (causative sense), so 'having caused to be ground'.
pisāpetvā.example_1: Athassa so sahāyako vāṇijo bahuṃ candanaṃ pisāpetvā pātiṃ pūretvā ‘‘ ehi, samma, yāva bhattaṃ pacati, tāva cetiyakaraṇaṭṭhānaṃ gantvā āgamissāmā ’’ ti taṃ ādāya tattha gantvā candanapūjaṃ akāsi.
pisāpetvā.translation_1: Then that merchant friend of his had much sandalwood ground up, filled a dish, and said, “Come, friend, while the rice is cooking, we shall go to the shrine-construction site and return.” He took him, went there, and performed a sandalwood offering.

palikhati.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text oṭṭhaṃ palikhati, 'licks the lips'. Some editions read parikhati; the commentary lists this among the forty feminine wiles.
palikhati.example_1: Sā theraṃ nisīdāpetvā ‘‘ cattālīsāya khalu, samma, puṇṇamukha ṭhānehi itthī purisaṃ accāvadati vijambhati vinamati gilasati vilajjati nakhena nakhaṃ ghaṭṭeti, pādena pādaṃ akkamati, kaṭṭhena pathaviṃ vilikhati, dārakaṃ ullaṅgheti olaṅgheti, kīḷati kīḷāpeti, cumbati cumbāpeti, bhuñjati bhuñjāpeti, dadāti āyācati, katamanukaroti, uccaṃ bhāsati, nīcaṃ bhāsati, aviccaṃ bhāsati, viviccaṃ bhāsati, naccena gītena vāditena roditena vilasitena vibhūsitena jagghati, pekkhati, kaṭiṃ cāleti, guyhabhaṇḍakaṃ cāleti, ūruṃ vivarati, ūruṃ pidahati, thanaṃ dasseti, kacchaṃ dasseti, nābhiṃ dasseti, akkhiṃ nikhaṇati, bhamukaṃ ukkhipati, oṭṭhaṃ palikhati, jivhaṃ nillāleti, dussaṃ muñcati, dussaṃ bandhati, sirasaṃ muñcati, sirasaṃ bandhatī ’’ ti (jā.2.21.300) evaṃ āgataṃ itthikuttaṃ itthilīlaṃ dassetvā tassa purato ṭhitā imaṃ gāthamāha –
palikhati.translation_1: Having seated the elder, she displayed the feminine gestures and feminine playfulness—as follows: “Friend, it is said that a woman accosts a man in forty ways: yawning, bowing down, gesticulating, making amorous glances, rubbing nails against nails, placing foot on foot, scratching the ground with a stick, lifting a boy, lowering a boy, playing herself, making a boy play, kissing, making a boy kiss, eating, making a boy eat, giving, begging, imitating him, speaking loudly, speaking softly, speaking openly, speaking privately, dancing, singing, playing instruments, weeping, gesturing, dressing up, laughing, staring, swaying hips, wiggling her hidden parts, baring thighs, covering thighs, displaying breasts, displaying armpits, displaying navels, blinking eyes, raising eyebrows, pursing lips, dangling tongue, taking off clothes, putting on clothes, untying hair, tying hair”—having displayed these, she stood before him and spoke this verse:

senakuṭumbiko.meaning_2: Sena the householder; the householder named Sena
senakuṭumbiko.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name of a householder in the Bandhumatī story. Nominative singular in the text. Could also be read as a compound meaning 'Sena's householder'.
senakuṭumbiko.example_1: Tesu vayappattakāle kuṭumbaṃ saṇṭhāpetvā viharantesu ‘‘ buddharatanaṃ loke uppannaṃ, dhammaratanaṃ, saṅgharatanaṃ, dānāni detha, puññāni karotha, ajja aṭṭhamī, ajja cātuddasī, ajja pannarasī, uposathaṃ karotha, dhammaṃ suṇāthā ’’ ti dhammaghosakassa bandhumatīnagare ghosanaṃ sutvā mahājanaṃ purebhattaṃ dānaṃ datvā pacchābhattaṃ dhammassavanāya gacchantaṃ disvā senakuṭumbiko ‘‘ kahaṃ gacchathā ’’ ti pucchitvā ‘‘ satthu santikaṃ dhammassavanāyā ’’ ti vutte ‘‘ ahampi gamissāmī ’’ ti tehi saddhiṃyeva gantvā parisapariyante nisīdi.
senakuṭumbiko.translation_1: When they grew up and were living their household life, Sena the householder heard the Dhamma-crier in Bandhumatī announce, “The Buddha-treasure has appeared, the Dhamma-treasure, the Saṅgha-treasure. Give alms, perform merit. Observe the Uposatha on the eighth, fourteenth, and fifteenth days. Listen to the Dhamma.” Seeing the multitude going to give alms before their meal and to hear the Dhamma after their meal, Sena the householder asked, “Where are you going?” and when they replied, “To the Teacher to hear the Dhamma,” he said, “I will go too,” and went along, sitting at the edge of the assembly.

sodhiyamāne.meaning_2: being cleaned; being purified; being cleared
sodhiyamāne.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative absolute with bhūmitale: 'while the ground was being cleared'. Passive of sodheti; the form shows -o- for -u- before the double consonant.
sodhiyamāne.example_1: Athassa vayappattakāle gehakaraṇatthāya bhūmitale sodhiyamāne sakkassa bhavanaṃ uṇhākāraṃ dassesi.
sodhiyamāne.translation_1: Later, when he had reached manhood and the ground was being cleared to build a house, it sent a warmth to Sakka’s heaven.

kaṭattho.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name of one of the seven guarding yakkhas at the gate-towers. Nominative singular in the text; the reading kaṭattho shows the ending -o on the stem kaṭattha. The split is uncertain.
kaṭattho.example_1: Paṭhame dvārakoṭṭhake yamakoḷī nāma yakkho attano parivārena yakkhasahassena saddhiṃ ārakkhaṃ gaṇhi, dutiye uppalo nāma attano parivārayakkhānaṃ dvīhi sahassehi saddhiṃ, tatiye vajiro nāma tīhi sahassehi saddhiṃ, catutthe vajirabāhu nāma catūhi sahassehi saddhiṃ, pañcame kasakando nāma pañcahi sahassehi saddhiṃ, chaṭṭhe kaṭattho nāma chahi sahassehi saddhiṃ, sattame disāmukho nāma sattahi sahassehi saddhiṃ ārakkhaṃ gaṇhi.
kaṭattho.translation_1: At the first gate-tower, the yakkha named Yamakoḷī guarded with his retinue of a thousand yakkhas; at the second, Uppala with two thousand; at the third, Vajira with three thousand; at the fourth, Vajirabāhu with four thousand; at the fifth, Kasakando with five thousand; at the sixth, Kaṭaṭṭha with six thousand; and at the seventh, Disāmukha with seven thousand.

mandībhūtesu.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative plural in the text, agreeing with manussesu. Formed from mandī (weak, slight) + bhūta (become).
mandībhūtesu.example_1: Aparabhāge yadicchakaṃ ādāya gatattā manussesu mandībhūtesu rājā jotikassa pitaraṃ āha –
mandībhūtesu.translation_1: Later, when people had taken what they wanted and the crowds had thinned, the king said to Jotika’s father:

paharitabbā.meaning_2: to be struck; should be struck; to be beaten
paharitabbā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Potential participle expressing obligation, used with akkositabbā vā paharitabbā vā in the text; nominative singular feminine agreeing with the implied object.
paharitabbā.example_1: Atha naṃ sā ‘‘ atisāhasikakammaṃ te kataṃ, mama kuddhena te ahameva akkositabbā vā paharitabbā vā, kasmā atītānāgatapaccuppannesu buddhesu veramakāsī ’’ ti āha.
paharitabbā.translation_1: Then she said, “You have committed a very reckless act; you should have scolded or struck me if you were angry at me, but why did you commit an offense against the Buddhas of the past, future, and present?”

paridahāpetvā.meaning_2: having caused to be dressed (in); having had (him) put on
paridahāpetvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative absolutive of paridahati (√dah with *āpe); the model gives √dah as the closest root. Here with dve rattavatthāni: the brahmins had Vaṅgīsa dressed in two red garments.
paridahāpetvā.example_1: Brāhmaṇā ‘‘ sakkā imaṃ nissāya lokaṃ khāditun ’’ ti cintetvā taṃ dve rattavatthāni paridahāpetvā ādāya janapadaṃ carantā manusse vadanti ‘‘ eso vaṅgīso nāma brāhmaṇo matamanussānaṃ sīsaṃ ākoṭetvā nibbattaṭṭhānaṃ jānāti, attano ñātakānaṃ nibbattaṭṭhānaṃ pucchathā ’’ ti.
paridahāpetvā.translation_1: Thinking, “We can make a living by relying on this brahmin,” the brahmins clothed him in two red robes and, taking him through the countryside, they told people: “This brahmin named Vaṅgīsa knows where those who have died have been reborn by rapping on their skulls; ask him about where your own relatives have been reborn.”

vosiko.meaning_2: having reached the end; having attained completion; having accomplished the finish
vosiko.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Related to vosāna (end, completion), as in vusitavosānaṃ and sabbavositavosānaṃ in the same passage; nominative singular qualifying the arahant.
vosiko.example_1: Tassattho – yo pubbenivāsaṃ pākaṭaṃ katvā jānāti, chabbīsatidevalokabhedaṃ saggañca catubbidhaṃ apāyañca dibbacakkhunā passati, atho jātikkhayasaṅkhātaṃ arahattaṃ patto, abhiññeyyaṃ dhammaṃ abhijānitvā pariññeyyaṃ parijānitvā pahātabbaṃ pahāya sacchikātabbaṃ sacchikatvā vosiko niṭṭhānaṃ patto, vusitavosānaṃ vā patto, āsavakkhayapaññāya monabhāvaṃ pattattā muni, tamahaṃ sabbesaṃ kilesānaṃ vosānaṃ arahattamaggañāṇaṃ brahmacariyavāsaṃ vutthabhāvena sabbavositavosānaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ vadāmīti.
vosiko.translation_1: Its meaning: Whoever knows past lives by making them evident, sees with divine eye the heaven and the four planes of misery, and has attained the end of birth—arahantship; having understood what should be understood, comprehended what should be comprehended, abandoned what should be abandoned, and realized what should be realized, having attained the finish, or having attained the perfection of accomplishments, and being a sage through the attainment of the 'muni' state via the knowledge of the destruction of taints—I proclaim that one a brahmin who has achieved the holy life of the arahant path-knowledge, which is the finish of all defilements.
